GDP.means: US nominal GDP growth year on year: real output growth plus inflation. It is the best single gauge of US revenue growth for companies selling into America.
GDP.watch: Nominal growth near 4% is normal; above 6% means inflation is still running hot; a fall below 3% usually comes with recession and weaker corporate spending.
GDP.links: Moves with US corporate earnings, nominal yields and S&P 500 revenue growth; Indian IT revenue growth tends to follow with a 2 to 4 quarter lag.

companies.why: largest US revenue share among Indian IT; client budgets track US activity
about 60% North America revenue; discretionary deals follow US growth
consulting-led, sensitive to US discretionary spend

GDPC1.means: US real GDP growth year on year, the output change after removing inflation.
GDPC1.watch: Two quarters of falling real GDP is the popular recession marker. Growth below 1% usually leads to IT deal delays, weaker export orders and lower US yields.
GDPC1.links: Leads US unemployment and lags financial conditions; drives demand for Indian IT, pharma generics volume, auto component and textile exports.

companies.why: largest US revenue share among Indian IT; client budgets track US activity
about 60% North America revenue; discretionary deals follow US growth
consulting-led, sensitive to US discretionary spend
US class 8 truck and industrial exports

CPIAUCSL.means: US consumer price inflation year on year, including food and energy.
CPIAUCSL.watch: The Fed targets 2% (on PCE). Headline above 3% keeps rate cuts off the table, holds US yields and the dollar up and tends to pull money out of emerging markets including India.
CPIAUCSL.links: Moves with oil and gasoline prices and the 10Y breakeven; leads Fed funds expectations and the 2Y yield.

companies.why: sticky US inflation keeps US yields high and drives FPI selling of Indian financials
higher US prices lift billing rates but squeeze client budgets

CPILFESL.means: US core CPI, excluding food and energy, the trend measure of US inflation.
CPILFESL.watch: Core above 3% signals sticky services and wage inflation; the Fed rarely cuts while core is rising.
CPILFESL.links: Lags wages and shelter costs; moves the 2Y Treasury yield and the dollar.

PCEPILFE.means: US core personal consumption expenditure price index, the Fed's preferred inflation measure.
PCEPILFE.watch: The Fed's target is 2%. Readings above 2.5% limit rate cuts, keep the dollar firm and tighten conditions for emerging market flows.
PCEPILFE.links: Runs about 0.3 to 0.5 pts below core CPI; leads Fed funds rate decisions.

UNRATE.means: US unemployment rate. Rising unemployment is the clearest sign the US cycle is turning.
UNRATE.watch: The Sahm rule: a 0.5 pt rise in the 3-month average above its 12-month low has marked every US recession. Rising unemployment means weaker US consumer and enterprise spending.
UNRATE.links: Lags GDP and jobless claims; a rising rate pulls down the 2Y yield and the dollar and tends to slow Indian IT hiring and deal flow.

companies.why: US layoffs and slower spending delay IT deals
collections and BPM work can rise in a downturn, but volumes in mortgages fall

ICSA.means: Weekly first-time claims for US unemployment benefits, the most timely US labour market indicator.
ICSA.watch: Sustained readings above about 300,000 have preceded past recessions; a fast rise of 50,000 or more over a few months is the warning sign.
ICSA.links: Leads the unemployment rate and payrolls by a few months; rising claims usually pull down US yields.

companies.why: rising layoffs signal weaker US enterprise budgets
deal ramp-ups slow when US hiring weakens

PAYEMS.means: Monthly change in US non-farm payroll jobs. Positive and steady means the US economy is adding jobs.
PAYEMS.watch: Above 150,000 a month is solid growth; below 50,000 or negative for several months signals a slowdown. Strong prints push yields and the dollar up and can hit EM flows.
PAYEMS.links: Moves with jobless claims (inverse) and leads consumer spending; big surprises move the 2Y yield and USD/INR on the day.

companies.why: steady US hiring supports IT services demand

HOUST.means: New US residential construction starts at an annual rate, a leading indicator of US housing and durable goods demand.
HOUST.watch: Starts fall first when mortgage rates rise; a drop below 1.2 million annualised has marked housing slumps. Housing drives furniture, flooring, home textiles and building products demand.
HOUST.links: Moves inversely with the 30Y mortgage rate with a lag of 3 to 9 months; leads US furnishing and appliance spending.

companies.why: towels and bed linen sold to US retailers track home sales and moves
mortgage BPM volumes rise with US housing activity

INDPRO.means: US industrial production growth: factory, mining and utility output year on year.
INDPRO.watch: Negative growth for several months signals industrial recession; it hits demand for Indian engineering and chemical exports.
INDPRO.links: Moves with the ISM manufacturing index and copper; leads US capex and freight volumes.

companies.why: mining and cement wear parts exports

DRCLACBS.means: Share of US consumer loans more than 30 days past due at commercial banks, a measure of household stress.
DRCLACBS.watch: Rising delinquency for several quarters signals a weakening US consumer, tighter lending and lower spending on goods and services.
DRCLACBS.links: Lags unemployment and interest rates; rises with high card balances and rates.

companies.why: collections and recovery work rises with delinquency
stressed US lenders cut discretionary tech spend

DRCCLACBS.means: Share of US credit card balances more than 30 days past due.
DRCCLACBS.watch: Card delinquency above about 4% has historically coincided with consumer recessions; a steady climb flags slowing US consumption.
DRCCLACBS.links: Leads consumer loan delinquency; moves with unemployment and card interest rates.

GFDEGDQ188S.means: US federal debt as a share of GDP.
GFDEGDQ188S.watch: Above 120% the debate on fiscal sustainability, term premium and Treasury supply intensifies; rising debt keeps long-term yields higher than otherwise.
GFDEGDQ188S.links: Drives Treasury issuance and term premium (30Y yield); a structural support for gold.

companies.why: fiscal worries support gold, lifting gold-loan collateral
higher gold prices lift value but slow volumes

FYFSGDA188S.means: US federal budget balance as a share of GDP; negative means deficit.
FYFSGDA188S.watch: Deficits above 5% of GDP outside recessions are unusual and add Treasury supply, which pushes up long-term yields.
FYFSGDA188S.links: Inverse of debt-to-GDP changes; wider deficits lift term premium and the 30Y yield.

VAPGDPMA.means: US manufacturing value added as a share of GDP.
VAPGDPMA.watch: A long decline reflects offshoring; a rise would signal reshoring and tariff-led substitution, a headwind for import suppliers and a chance for China plus one suppliers.
VAPGDPMA.links: Moves with US industrial policy and tariffs; relevant for Indian electronics and engineering exporters.

companies.why: China plus one gains vs US reshoring
supplies US industrial and defence supply chains

M2SL.means: US broad money supply growth year on year.
M2SL.watch: M2 contracted in 2023 for the first time since the 1930s; renewed growth above 5% tends to support risk assets and emerging market flows.
M2SL.links: Leads nominal GDP and asset prices with a lag; moves with Fed balance sheet and bank lending.

WALCL.means: Total assets on the Federal Reserve balance sheet. Rising means quantitative easing; falling means quantitative tightening.
WALCL.watch: QT drains dollar liquidity; markets watch for the point where bank reserves become scarce and repo rates spike, which forces the Fed to stop.
WALCL.links: Main input to US net liquidity; correlates with the S&P 500, Bitcoin and EM equity flows.

companies.why: global liquidity supports FPI inflows into Indian large caps

WTREGEN.means: The US Treasury's cash balance at the Fed (TGA). A rising balance drains reserves from banks; a falling one adds them.
WTREGEN.watch: Big rebuilds after debt-ceiling deals drained several hundred billion dollars and coincided with weaker risk assets.
WTREGEN.links: Subtracts from net liquidity; moves with tax dates and Treasury issuance.

RRPONTSYD.means: Money parked at the Fed's overnight reverse repo facility by money market funds.
RRPONTSYD.watch: Near zero means the excess-liquidity buffer is used up, so further QT or TGA rebuilds drain bank reserves directly.
RRPONTSYD.links: Subtracts from net liquidity; falls when T-bill yields exceed the RRP rate.

DFF.means: Effective federal funds rate, the overnight rate the Fed sets.
DFF.watch: The gap between US and Indian policy rates matters for carry trades: a narrower gap makes the rupee more vulnerable and reduces RBI room to cut.
DFF.links: Leads the 2Y Treasury yield, the dollar and mortgage rates; cuts usually weaken the dollar and help EM flows.

companies.why: higher US rates reduce FPI appetite for Indian financials
higher global rates raise wholesale funding costs
rate hikes slow US spending but strengthen the dollar

DGS2.means: US 2-year Treasury yield, the market's view of Fed policy over the next two years.
DGS2.watch: Moves above the Fed funds rate signal hikes are expected; sharp falls price in cuts. Big moves shift USD/INR and FPI debt flows.
DGS2.links: Leads the Fed funds rate; drives the dollar and the 10Y minus 2Y curve.

DGS10.means: US 10-year Treasury yield, the global risk-free benchmark for valuing long-duration assets.
DGS10.watch: A move toward 5% has repeatedly triggered equity drawdowns and EM outflows; a narrowing gap to India's 10Y (below 2.5 pts) reduces FPI interest in Indian bonds and pressures the rupee.
DGS10.links: Moves with real yields and breakeven inflation; inversely with growth stocks and gold; leads FPI debt flows into India.

companies.why: rising US yields trigger FPI selling in Indian banks
high-multiple financials de-rate when discount rates rise
neutral on demand, helped if the dollar firms

DGS30.means: US 30-year Treasury yield, sensitive to long-run inflation expectations and fiscal supply.
DGS30.watch: Rising 30Y yields with stable short rates (bear steepening) signal fiscal or term premium worries, often bad for equities and EM.
DGS30.links: Moves with term premium, deficits and mortgage rates.

T10Y2Y.means: US 10Y yield minus 2Y yield, the shape of the yield curve.
T10Y2Y.watch: Inversion (below zero) has preceded every US recession since the 1970s; recessions usually begin after the curve re-steepens out of inversion.
T10Y2Y.links: Steepens when the Fed cuts (2Y falls) or when term premium rises (10Y rises).

companies.why: steeper global curves are read as better for bank margins, but recession signals hurt

DFII10.means: US 10Y inflation-protected (TIPS) yield, the real cost of long-term money.
DFII10.watch: Real yields above 2% are restrictive and typically pressure gold, growth stocks and EM assets; falling real yields help gold.
DFII10.links: Gold has historically moved inversely with real yields, though central bank buying weakened the link after 2022.

companies.why: higher real yields usually weigh on gold prices
lower gold prices help jewellery volumes
high real yields pull FPI money back to the US

T10YIE.means: US 10Y breakeven inflation: nominal minus TIPS yield, the bond market's average inflation expectation.
T10YIE.watch: Above 2.5% signals markets doubt the Fed's 2% target; usually rises with oil prices.
T10YIE.links: Moves with crude oil, commodity prices and headline CPI.

MORTGAGE30US.watch: Above 7% sharply reduces home sales and refinancing; falls below 6% have unlocked housing turnover.
MORTGAGE30US.links: Tracks the 10Y yield plus a spread; inversely leads housing starts and home-related spending.

companies.why: high mortgage rates cut US home moves and home-textile demand

BAMLH0A0HYM2.means: Extra yield on US high-yield (junk) bonds over Treasuries, a gauge of default risk and risk appetite.
BAMLH0A0HYM2.watch: Below 3.5 pts is complacent; a jump above 5 pts signals stress and above 8 pts recession. Widening spreads usually come with EM equity outflows.
BAMLH0A0HYM2.links: Moves with VIX and inversely with the S&P 500; widening often leads equity drawdowns.

companies.why: global risk-off triggers FPI selling of liquid Indian large caps
wider global spreads raise NBFC funding costs

BAMLC0A0CM.means: Extra yield on US investment-grade corporate bonds over Treasuries.
BAMLC0A0CM.watch: Below 1 pt is tight; above 1.5 pts signals tightening credit conditions; above 2 pts stress.
BAMLC0A0CM.links: Moves with HY spreads but less violently; widens with Treasury volatility (MOVE).

BAMLH0A3HYC.means: Spread on CCC-rated and lower US bonds, the riskiest credit tier.
BAMLH0A3HYC.watch: Moves first and furthest in credit stress; a rise of 3 pts or more in a few months flags rising defaults.
BAMLH0A3HYC.links: Leads broader HY spreads; widens with rate hikes and slowing growth.

BAMLEMCBPIOAS.means: Option-adjusted spread on emerging market corporate bonds over Treasuries.
BAMLEMCBPIOAS.watch: Widening signals EM risk aversion and makes dollar borrowing costlier for Indian corporates issuing abroad.
BAMLEMCBPIOAS.links: Moves with the dollar, US HY spreads and EM equity flows.

companies.why: regular dollar bond issuer; wider spreads raise refinancing cost

IRLTLT01FRM156N.means: France 10-year government bond yield, monthly average.
IRLTLT01FRM156N.watch: Matters mainly through its spread to Germany: political or fiscal stress in France widens it and can spill into euro weakness.
IRLTLT01FRM156N.links: Moves with German Bunds plus a fiscal risk premium.

IRLTLT01DEM156N.means: Germany 10-year Bund yield, the euro area risk-free benchmark.
IRLTLT01DEM156N.watch: Rising Bund yields with large German fiscal spending tighten global financial conditions and pull global bond yields up.
IRLTLT01DEM156N.links: Moves with US 10Y and ECB policy; drives EUR/USD.

companies.why: European revenue converts at EUR/INR; higher Bund yields often mean a firmer euro

IRLTLT01JPM156N.watch: Rising JGB yields can pull Japanese money home from global bonds and unwind yen carry trades, which in past episodes (August 2024) hit EM equities including India within days.
IRLTLT01JPM156N.links: Moves with Bank of Japan policy and USD/JPY; a rising JGB yield with a strengthening yen signals carry unwind risk.

companies.why: carry-trade unwinds trigger FPI selling of liquid large caps

IRLTLT01GBM156N.watch: Spikes signal fiscal credibility stress (2022 mini-budget); gilts often lead global long-end selloffs.
IRLTLT01GBM156N.links: Moves with US 10Y and UK inflation; affects GBP/USD.

INDIRLTLT01STM.means: India 10-year government bond yield, monthly average: the benchmark cost of long-term money in India.
INDIRLTLT01STM.watch: The spread over the repo rate and over the US 10Y matter. A gap to US 10Y below about 2.5 pts reduces foreign interest in Indian bonds. Falling yields lift bank treasury gains and rate-sensitive sectors.
INDIRLTLT01STM.links: Moves with RBI repo rate, CPI, fiscal deficit, crude oil and FPI debt flows; leads corporate bond and home loan rates.

companies.why: falling yields give treasury gains on a large bond book
PSU banks hold large government bond portfolios
falling yields lift bond values but compress new business guarantees
lower bond yields cut NBFC funding costs
bond-funded lender benefits from lower yields

DTWEXBGS.means: The Fed's broad trade-weighted dollar index against major trading partners including emerging markets.
DTWEXBGS.watch: A rising broad dollar tightens global financial conditions, pressures EM currencies including the rupee and tends to coincide with FPI outflows from India.
DTWEXBGS.links: Moves with US real yields and inversely with commodities and EM equities.

companies.why: dollar revenue, rupee costs: weaker rupee lifts margins
each 1% rupee depreciation adds roughly 20 to 30 bps to margin
strong dollar periods bring FPI selling
a strong dollar usually lowers global metal prices

DCOILBRENTEU.means: Brent crude spot price in dollars per barrel. India imports about 85% of its oil, so Brent is the single most important commodity for India.
DCOILBRENTEU.watch: Brent above $90 to $100 raises freight and logistics costs, widens India's current account deficit, weakens the rupee and lifts CPI and WPI with a lag; each $10 rise adds roughly 0.4% of GDP to the import bill.
DCOILBRENTEU.links: Moves with the dollar (inverse), global growth and OPEC supply; leads India WPI, CPI fuel, USD/INR and the trade deficit.

companies.why: crude realisation rises (capped by windfall tax when high)
marketing margins shrink if pump prices lag crude
crude derivatives are about a third of raw materials
jet fuel is about 40% of costs
synthetic rubber and carbon black are crude-linked

DCOILWTICO.means: WTI crude spot price, the US benchmark.
DCOILWTICO.watch: WTI usually trades a few dollars below Brent; a wider gap reflects US supply gluts or export constraints.
DCOILWTICO.links: Moves with Brent, US crude inventories and the SPR; India's import basket is Brent and Dubai-linked, so Brent matters more.

companies.why: crude realisation rises (capped by windfall tax when high)
marketing margins shrink if pump prices lag crude

DEXINUS.means: Rupees per US dollar from the Fed's H.10 series, used for long history. Rising means a weaker rupee.
DEXINUS.watch: Fast depreciation (more than 3 to 4% in a quarter) raises imported inflation, prompts RBI intervention and drains reserves; a weak rupee helps exporters and hurts importers.
DEXINUS.links: Moves with crude oil, the dollar index, FPI flows and the current account deficit.

companies.why: dollar revenue, rupee costs: weaker rupee lifts margins
each 1% rupee depreciation adds roughly 20 to 30 bps to margin
large US and export revenue in dollars
US generics revenue converts to more rupees
marketing margins shrink when crude rises faster than retail prices
most marketing-heavy OMC, so most exposed to crude spikes

BAA10Y.means: Moody's Baa corporate yield minus the 10Y Treasury, a credit spread series going back to 1986.
BAA10Y.watch: Spikes above 3 pts marked 2001, 2008 and 2020; long-run average is about 2.3 pts.
BAA10Y.links: Moves with HY spreads and recessions; useful for long history comparison.

AAA10Y.means: Moody's Aaa corporate yield minus the 10Y Treasury, the spread on the safest corporate bonds.
AAA10Y.watch: Rises during flight-to-quality episodes; less sensitive to defaults than Baa.
AAA10Y.links: The Baa minus Aaa gap measures pure credit risk.

NETLIQ.means: Fed assets minus the Treasury cash balance minus reverse repo: a rough measure of dollar liquidity reaching markets.
NETLIQ.watch: Rising net liquidity has tended to coincide with rising equities and EM inflows; sharp falls with risk-off periods.
NETLIQ.links: Moves with the S&P 500, Nasdaq and Bitcoin with a short lag; inversely with the dollar.

companies.why: high-beta financial favoured in liquidity upswings

FRDE.watch: Above 1 pt signals political or fiscal stress in France; spikes can weaken the euro.
FRDE.links: Moves with French politics and euro area risk.

GDPLVL.means: Level of US nominal GDP in trillions of dollars at an annual rate, used as the denominator for debt and market value ratios.
GDPLVL.watch: Watch the growth rate rather than the level; a stalling level signals recession.
GDPLVL.links: Drives US tax receipts and debt ratios; denominator for market cap to GDP and debt to GDP.

WCESTUS1.means: US commercial crude oil inventories, excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, weekly from EIA.
WCESTUS1.watch: Draws larger than seasonal norms signal tight markets and support prices; big builds signal oversupply.
WCESTUS1.links: Moves inversely with WTI and Brent prices and with refinery runs.

WCSSTUS1.watch: Large releases (2022) dampen price spikes; refilling adds demand. A low SPR reduces the US buffer against supply shocks.
WCSSTUS1.links: Releases cap crude prices short term; refills support them.

Y:^NSEI.means: Nifty 50, India's benchmark of the 50 largest liquid NSE stocks, weighted by free-float market cap.
Y:^NSEI.watch: Drawdowns of 10% or more have usually come with FPI selling, oil spikes or global risk-off; financials are about a third of the index, so bank earnings dominate.
Y:^NSEI.links: Moves with FPI equity flows, USD/INR (inverse), Brent (inverse) and global equities; domestic SIP flows cushion falls.

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly
AUM and fees rise with equity values

Y:^CRSLDX.means: Nifty 500, covering about 95% of NSE free-float market cap: the broad Indian market.
Y:^CRSLDX.watch: Divergence from Nifty 50 shows whether rallies are broad or narrow.
Y:^CRSLDX.links: Moves with Nifty 50 plus mid and small cap behaviour; domestic flows matter more here.

companies.why: broad market rallies lift mutual fund AUM

Y:^NSEMDCP50.watch: Midcaps typically fall 1.3 to 1.5 times as much as Nifty in corrections.
Y:^NSEMDCP50.links: Moves with domestic flows, retail activity and risk appetite.

Y:^BSESN.means: BSE Sensex, the 30-stock benchmark with history from 1979.
Y:^BSESN.watch: Useful for long history; moves almost identically to the Nifty 50.

Y:^INDIAVIX.means: India VIX: expected 30-day Nifty volatility from option prices, the Indian fear gauge.
Y:^INDIAVIX.watch: Below 12 signals complacency; above 20 signals stress and above 25 panic, usually near election results or global shocks. High VIX raises option premiums and trading volumes.
Y:^INDIAVIX.links: Moves inversely with Nifty; spikes with US VIX, FPI selling and event risk.

companies.why: volatility lifts options volumes and premium turnover
higher activity, but retail losses can cut participation

Y:^NSEBANK.means: Nifty Bank: the 12 most liquid bank stocks, dominated by HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank.
Y:^NSEBANK.watch: Banks drive about a third of Nifty; outperformance usually signals confidence in credit growth and asset quality.
Y:^NSEBANK.links: Moves with credit growth, net interest margins, bond yields and FPI flows.

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly
high foreign holding, sensitive to flow swings

Y:^CNXIT.means: Nifty IT: Indian IT services exporters.
Y:^CNXIT.watch: Tracks US tech spending and the rupee; derates when US recession fears rise or AI disrupts services pricing.
Y:^CNXIT.links: Moves with Nasdaq, US GDP and USD/INR; often defensive in domestic slowdowns.

Y:^CNXPHARMA.watch: Defensive in risk-off; sensitive to US generic pricing, FDA inspections and US tariffs.
Y:^CNXPHARMA.links: Moves with USD/INR and US generic price erosion; low correlation with banks.

Y:^CNXAUTO.means: Nifty Auto: vehicle and auto component makers.
Y:^CNXAUTO.watch: Leads the consumption cycle; hurt by rising steel, rubber and fuel prices and helped by rate cuts and good monsoons.
Y:^CNXAUTO.links: Moves with vehicle loan growth, rural income and commodity costs (inverse).

Y:^CNXFMCG.watch: Defensive; underperforms when food and palm oil inflation squeezes margins and when rural demand is weak.
Y:^CNXFMCG.links: Moves inversely with commodity inflation; relative strength rises in market sell-offs.

Y:^CNXMETAL.means: Nifty Metal: steel, aluminium, zinc and mining stocks.
Y:^CNXMETAL.watch: Highly cyclical; tracks China demand, LME prices and Indian safeguard duties.
Y:^CNXMETAL.links: Moves with copper, the copper/gold ratio and China stimulus; inversely with the dollar.

Y:^CNXENERGY.means: Nifty Energy: oil, gas, power and coal companies.
Y:^CNXENERGY.watch: Mixed exposure to crude: upstream gains and refiners and marketers lose; power utilities add defensiveness.
Y:^CNXENERGY.links: Moves with power demand, crude and government capex.

Y:^CNXREALTY.watch: Highest beta sector; driven by housing sales, home loan rates and land prices.
Y:^CNXREALTY.links: Moves with housing credit, bond yields (inverse) and Nifty with about 1.5 times beta.

Y:^CNXINFRA.means: Nifty Infrastructure: telecom, power, construction, cement and ports.
Y:^CNXINFRA.watch: Tracks government and private capex cycles.
Y:^CNXINFRA.links: Moves with IIP capital goods, GFCF growth and government capex.

Y:^CNXPSUBANK.watch: Sensitive to bond yields (treasury gains), credit costs and government policy; rallies when asset quality improves.
Y:^CNXPSUBANK.links: Moves with MSME and agriculture credit, bond yields (inverse) and recapitalisation news.

Y:^CNXPSE.means: Nifty PSE: listed public sector enterprises.
Y:^CNXPSE.watch: Driven by government capex, defence orders, dividends and divestment.
Y:^CNXPSE.links: Moves with oil and coal prices and government spending.

Y:^CNXCONSUM.means: Nifty India Consumption: consumer goods, autos, retail, telecom and leisure.
Y:^CNXCONSUM.watch: Tracks private consumption; underperforms when inflation erodes real incomes.
Y:^CNXCONSUM.links: Moves with PFCE, CPI (inverse) and personal loan growth.

Y:^GSPC.means: S&P 500: 500 large US companies, the global risk benchmark.
Y:^GSPC.watch: Corrections of 10% or more tend to bring FPI selling in India within days; rallies help EM risk appetite.
Y:^GSPC.links: Moves with US earnings, real yields (inverse) and liquidity; Nifty correlation is moderate and rises in sell-offs.

companies.why: largest US revenue share among Indian IT; client budgets track US activity
about 60% North America revenue; discretionary deals follow US growth

Y:^IXIC.watch: Tech drawdowns hurt Indian IT sentiment and digital platforms' valuations.
Y:^IXIC.links: Moves with real yields (inverse) and AI capex.

companies.why: Indian internet valuations track global tech

Y:^RUT.means: Russell 2000: US small caps, sensitive to domestic US growth and floating-rate debt.
Y:^RUT.watch: Outperformance signals broadening of the US rally and expectations of rate cuts.
Y:^RUT.links: Moves inversely with US 2Y yields and credit spreads.

Y:ACWI.means: MSCI All Country World Index ETF: global developed plus emerging equities.
Y:ACWI.watch: The benchmark most global funds measure against; India's weight in it drives passive flows.
Y:ACWI.links: Moves mostly with the US, which is about 60% of the index.

Y:EEM.watch: EM rallies usually come with a weaker dollar and China strength; India competes with China, Taiwan and Korea for EM allocations.
Y:EEM.links: Moves inversely with DXY; heavily weighted to China, Taiwan, India and Korea.

Y:RSP.means: Equal-weight S&P 500 ETF: every stock gets the same weight.
Y:RSP.watch: Weak equal-weight versus cap-weight means market leadership is narrow.
Y:RSP.links: Moves with US small and midcaps and cyclicals.

Y:^STOXX50E.means: Euro Stoxx 50: large euro area companies.
Y:^STOXX50E.watch: Europe is about 30% of Indian IT revenue; weak European equities often reflect weak euro demand.
Y:^STOXX50E.links: Moves with EUR/USD, Bund yields and China demand.

Y:^N225.watch: Driven by the yen and BOJ policy; sharp falls with yen strength have marked carry-trade unwinds.

Y:^HSI.means: Hang Seng: Hong Kong-listed Chinese companies.
Y:^HSI.watch: China rallies on stimulus can pull EM funds away from India; China weakness sometimes redirects flows to India.
Y:^HSI.links: Moves with China credit, property and US-China relations.

companies.why: China rallies pull EM allocation from India

Y:000001.SS.watch: Reflects domestic Chinese policy support and liquidity.
Y:000001.SS.links: Moves with Chinese credit growth and stimulus.

companies.why: China demand sets global steel prices

Y:^KS11.means: KOSPI, South Korea's benchmark, dominated by memory chip makers.
Y:^KS11.watch: A bellwether for global tech and trade cycles; foreigners treat Korea and India as alternative EM allocations.
Y:^KS11.links: Moves with semiconductor prices, USD/KRW (inverse) and global trade.

Y:^BVSP.means: Bovespa, Brazil's benchmark, heavy in commodities and banks.
Y:^BVSP.watch: Moves with iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
Y:^BVSP.links: Correlates with commodity prices and the real.

Y:EWZ.watch: Captures both stocks and currency; a commodity and carry play.
Y:EWZ.links: Moves with iron ore, oil and USD/BRL (inverse).

companies.why: largest crop protection market is Brazil

Y:ECH.means: Chile equities in US dollars (ETF), a copper and lithium proxy.
Y:ECH.watch: Rises with copper prices and EM risk appetite.

Y:EPU.means: Peru equities in US dollars (ETF), a copper, gold and silver mining proxy.

Y:ARGT.watch: Driven by Argentine reform politics and the peso.

Y:EWW.watch: Sensitive to US trade policy and nearshoring.
Y:EWW.links: Moves with the peso and US manufacturing.

Y:INDA.means: MSCI India ETF in US dollars: how a dollar-based foreign investor experiences Indian equities.
Y:INDA.watch: Combines Nifty performance and rupee moves; weakness versus EEM signals FPIs rotating out of India.
Y:INDA.links: Moves with Nifty and inversely with USD/INR.

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly

Y:SMH.means: VanEck semiconductor ETF, a proxy for the global chip cycle and AI hardware spending.
Y:SMH.watch: Semiconductor booms lift electronics supply chains; busts cut orders.
Y:SMH.links: Moves with Nvidia, Nasdaq and AI capex.

Y:NVDA.means: Nvidia share price, the bellwether of AI compute spending.
Y:NVDA.watch: Its results set the tone for AI capex expectations globally.
Y:NVDA.links: Moves with hyperscaler capex and SMH.

Y:AAPL.watch: Apple's shift of iPhone assembly to India (mostly unlisted contract makers) supports electronics exports and the component ecosystem.
Y:AAPL.links: Moves with US consumer tech demand and Nasdaq.

Y:MSFT.means: Microsoft share price, a proxy for enterprise software and cloud spending.
Y:MSFT.watch: Cloud and AI spending signals affect Indian IT deal pipelines.
Y:MSFT.links: Moves with enterprise IT budgets and AI capex.

companies.why: largest US revenue share among Indian IT; client budgets track US activity
about 60% North America revenue; discretionary deals follow US growth

Y:GOOGL.watch: Ad revenue tracks the global digital economy; its India GCC and capex plans matter for data centres.
Y:GOOGL.links: Moves with digital ad spend and AI.

Y:AMZN.means: Amazon share price; AWS and US retail.
Y:AMZN.watch: AWS capex and US retail demand both matter for India: cloud migration work and exporters.
Y:AMZN.links: Moves with US consumer and cloud spending.

companies.why: largest US revenue share among Indian IT; client budgets track US activity
about 60% North America revenue; discretionary deals follow US growth

Y:META.watch: Ad spending and AI capex bellwether.
Y:META.links: Moves with digital ad cycle and Nasdaq.

Y:ORCL.means: Oracle share price, a leveraged bet on AI data centre contracts.
Y:ORCL.watch: Large debt-funded AI capex makes it a gauge of AI financing stress.
Y:ORCL.links: Moves with AI capex sentiment and credit spreads.

Y:CRWV.means: CoreWeave share price, an AI cloud provider funded with heavy debt.
Y:CRWV.watch: Treated as a canary for AI infrastructure financing; sharp falls signal stress in AI capex funding.
Y:CRWV.links: Moves with Nvidia, credit spreads and AI sentiment.

Y:^VIX.watch: Below 15 is calm; above 25 is stress and above 35 panic. VIX spikes usually bring FPI selling and a jump in India VIX.
Y:^VIX.links: Moves inversely with the S&P 500 and with HY spreads.

Y:^MOVE.means: Implied volatility of US Treasuries, the bond market's fear gauge.
Y:^MOVE.watch: Above 120 signals rate stress (2022, March 2023 bank crisis); high MOVE tends to tighten financial conditions and widen EM spreads.
Y:^MOVE.links: Often leads the VIX; moves with Fed uncertainty and Treasury liquidity.

Y:DX-Y.NYB.means: US Dollar Index (DXY): the dollar against six major currencies, mostly the euro.
Y:DX-Y.NYB.watch: DXY above 105 has coincided with EM stress; falls below 100 usually help EM flows and commodities.
Y:DX-Y.NYB.links: Inversely tracks EUR/USD and gold; moves with US 2Y yield differentials.

companies.why: dollar strength comes with FPI outflows
metals priced in dollars tend to fall
aluminium prices weaken with a strong dollar

Y:USDINR=X.means: Rupees per US dollar, market rate. Rising means the rupee is weakening.
Y:USDINR=X.watch: RBI smooths volatility using reserves; sharp moves come with crude spikes, FPI outflows or a strong dollar. A weaker rupee raises import costs for oil, electronics, gold and coal, lifting CPI with a lag, and raises the rupee cost of dollar debt.
Y:USDINR=X.links: Moves with DXY, crude oil, FPI equity and debt flows and the US-India yield gap; inversely with forex reserves.

companies.why: dollar revenue, rupee costs: weaker rupee lifts margins
each 1% rupee depreciation adds roughly 20 to 30 bps to margin
large US and export revenue in dollars
US generics revenue converts to more rupees
crude is bought in dollars; rupee cost rises
aircraft leases and fuel are dollar-linked

Y:USDCNY=X.means: Chinese yuan per US dollar. Rising means a weaker yuan.
Y:USDCNY=X.watch: Yuan weakness exports deflation: cheaper Chinese steel, chemicals and electronics flood markets including India.
Y:USDCNY=X.links: Moves with China growth, US-China rate gap and trade tensions.

companies.why: cheaper Chinese steel exports pressure Indian prices

Y:USDJPY=X.means: Japanese yen per US dollar. Rising means a weaker yen.
Y:USDJPY=X.watch: A rapid fall in USD/JPY (yen strength) has triggered global carry unwinds; Japanese intervention is likely near historic weak-yen levels.
Y:USDJPY=X.links: Moves with the US-Japan yield gap; inversely with JPY/INR.

Y:EURUSD=X.means: US dollars per euro. Rising means a stronger euro and weaker dollar.
Y:EURUSD=X.watch: Euro strength usually means a softer dollar, which helps EM flows; it also lifts the rupee value of Europe-earned revenue.
Y:EURUSD=X.links: Inverse of DXY; moves with Germany-US yield gap.

companies.why: about 30% of revenue from Europe and UK

Y:USDKRW=X.means: Korean won per US dollar, a proxy for Asian tech-export sentiment.
Y:USDKRW=X.watch: Won weakness often reflects risk-off in Asian tech and semiconductor cycles.
Y:USDKRW=X.links: Moves with KOSPI (inverse), semiconductor prices and the dollar.

Y:USDBRL=X.watch: A carry-trade favourite; sharp real weakness signals EM risk-off.
Y:USDBRL=X.links: Moves with commodity prices (inverse) and Brazilian fiscal risk.

companies.why: Brazil is its largest crop protection market; a weaker real lowers rupee revenue

Y:GBPUSD=X.watch: Sterling weakness lowers the rupee value of UK revenues for Indian IT and auto companies with UK operations.
Y:GBPUSD=X.links: Moves with UK gilt yields and the Bank of England.

companies.why: Jaguar Land Rover earns in sterling

Y:BZ=F.means: Brent crude spot price in dollars per barrel. India imports about 85% of its oil, so Brent is the single most important commodity for India.
Y:BZ=F.watch: Brent above $90 to $100 raises freight and logistics costs, widens India's current account deficit, weakens the rupee and lifts CPI and WPI with a lag; each $10 rise adds roughly 0.4% of GDP to the import bill.
Y:BZ=F.links: Moves with the dollar (inverse), global growth and OPEC supply; leads India WPI, CPI fuel, USD/INR and the trade deficit.

companies.why: crude realisation rises (capped by windfall tax when high)
marketing margins shrink if pump prices lag crude
crude derivatives are about a third of raw materials
jet fuel is about 40% of costs
synthetic rubber and carbon black are crude-linked

Y:CL=F.means: WTI crude spot price, the US benchmark.
Y:CL=F.watch: WTI usually trades a few dollars below Brent; a wider gap reflects US supply gluts or export constraints.
Y:CL=F.links: Moves with Brent, US crude inventories and the SPR; India's import basket is Brent and Dubai-linked, so Brent matters more.

companies.why: crude realisation rises (capped by windfall tax when high)
marketing margins shrink if pump prices lag crude

Y:NG=F.means: US Henry Hub natural gas futures, dollars per million BTU.
Y:NG=F.watch: Henry Hub sets the cost of US LNG exports; GAIL has Henry Hub-linked LNG contracts, so a low price versus Asian spot is favourable for it.
Y:NG=F.links: Moves with US weather and LNG export demand; feeds into Asian LNG prices with shipping costs.

companies.why: its US LNG contracts are priced off Henry Hub
regasification volumes rise when LNG is cheap
costlier gas squeezes city gas margins
gas cost is passed through via subsidy

Y:GC=F.means: Gold futures price in dollars per ounce. In India, gold is both a savings asset and a large import item.
Y:GC=F.watch: Sharp rises raise India's gold import bill and current account deficit; they also boost the collateral value of gold loans and household wealth. Central bank buying has supported prices since 2022.
Y:GC=F.links: Moves inversely with US real yields and the dollar, and with geopolitical risk; leads India's gold imports in value terms.

companies.why: higher gold value lifts loan-to-value headroom and AUM
gold loan AUM and collateral cover rise with gold
gold loans are its largest book
inventory gains and higher ticket size, but grams sold fall when gold spikes
higher realisation per piece, weaker volumes at very high prices

Y:SI=F.means: Silver futures price in dollars per ounce; half industrial (solar, electronics), half precious metal.
Y:SI=F.watch: Silver tends to outperform gold late in risk-on cycles and fall harder in downturns.
Y:SI=F.links: Moves with gold and with industrial demand, especially solar panels.

companies.why: India's largest silver producer; silver is a big share of profit
silver paste is a solar cell input

Y:HG=F.means: Copper futures price in dollars per pound, a barometer of global industrial demand.
Y:HG=F.watch: Rising copper signals stronger global manufacturing and grid investment; it raises input costs for Indian wire, cable and electrical makers.
Y:HG=F.links: Moves with China activity, the dollar (inverse) and power grid and data centre spending.

companies.why: copper miner: realisation tracks LME price
copper is the main input; pass-through with a lag
copper used in wires, fans and motors

Y:ZW=F.means: Chicago wheat futures, a global grain price benchmark.
Y:ZW=F.watch: Spikes (2022) feed food inflation and can prompt export restrictions; India's domestic wheat price is set more by its own procurement and stocks.
Y:ZW=F.links: Moves with weather, Black Sea supply and the dollar.

companies.why: wheat flour is a key biscuit input
agri trading gains, but flour costs for foods

Y:URA.means: ETF of uranium miners, a proxy for sentiment on nuclear power.
Y:URA.watch: Rising prices reflect new reactor plans and supply constraints.
Y:URA.links: Moves with uranium spot prices and AI-driven power demand narratives.

companies.why: nuclear expansion plans, but fuel cost rises

Y:BTC-USD.means: Bitcoin price in US dollars, a speculative asset sensitive to global liquidity.
Y:BTC-USD.watch: Big moves tend to track liquidity cycles and risk appetite; crashes often coincide with leveraged retail losses.
Y:BTC-USD.links: Moves with US net liquidity and Nasdaq.

Y:^TNX.means: US 10-year Treasury yield, the global risk-free benchmark for valuing long-duration assets.
Y:^TNX.watch: A move toward 5% has repeatedly triggered equity drawdowns and EM outflows; a narrowing gap to India's 10Y (below 2.5 pts) reduces FPI interest in Indian bonds and pressures the rupee.
Y:^TNX.links: Moves with real yields and breakeven inflation; inversely with growth stocks and gold; leads FPI debt flows into India.

companies.why: rising US yields trigger FPI selling in Indian banks
high-multiple financials de-rate when discount rates rise
neutral on demand, helped if the dollar firms

Y:CNYINR=X.means: Rupees per Chinese yuan. Rising means the rupee is weaker against the yuan.
Y:CNYINR=X.watch: A weaker yuan versus the rupee makes Chinese imports cheaper, hurting Indian makers of chemicals, steel, solar modules and electronics that compete with China.
Y:CNYINR=X.links: Moves with USD/CNY and USD/INR; yuan devaluations (2015) triggered EM selloffs.

companies.why: a stronger yuan makes Chinese specialty chemicals less competitive

Y:JPYINR=X.means: Rupees per 100 Japanese yen. Rising means the yen is strengthening against the rupee.
Y:JPYINR=X.watch: A sharply stronger yen often signals carry-trade unwinding and global risk-off; it also raises the cost of yen loans and Japanese components.
Y:JPYINR=X.links: Moves with USD/JPY (inverse) and Japan yields.

companies.why: royalty to Suzuki and some imported parts are yen-linked

NSE:Nifty 50.means: Nifty 50, India's benchmark of the 50 largest liquid NSE stocks, weighted by free-float market cap.
NSE:Nifty 50.watch: Drawdowns of 10% or more have usually come with FPI selling, oil spikes or global risk-off; financials are about a third of the index, so bank earnings dominate.
NSE:Nifty 50.links: Moves with FPI equity flows, USD/INR (inverse), Brent (inverse) and global equities; domestic SIP flows cushion falls.

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly
AUM and fees rise with equity values

NSE:Nifty 500.means: Nifty 500, covering about 95% of NSE free-float market cap: the broad Indian market.
NSE:Nifty 500.watch: Divergence from Nifty 50 shows whether rallies are broad or narrow.
NSE:Nifty 500.links: Moves with Nifty 50 plus mid and small cap behaviour; domestic flows matter more here.

companies.why: broad market rallies lift mutual fund AUM

NSE:Nifty Midcap 100.means: Nifty Midcap 100: the midcap segment of Indian equities (stocks ranked about 101 to 250 by market cap).
NSE:Nifty Midcap 100.watch: Midcaps outperform in liquidity-driven, domestic-growth phases and underperform when valuations stretch or FPIs sell; their premium to Nifty valuations is the key risk gauge.
NSE:Nifty Midcap 100.links: Moves with retail and SIP flows, India VIX (inverse) and the Nifty / Midcap ratio (inverse).

companies.why: retail trading activity rises with broad rallies

NSE:Nifty Smallcap 100.means: Nifty Smallcap 100: the smallcap segment of Indian equities.
NSE:Nifty Smallcap 100.watch: Smallcaps can fall 30 to 60% in bear phases (2008, 2018 to 2020); froth signs are heavy IPO supply, retail F&O activity and regulatory warnings.
NSE:Nifty Smallcap 100.links: Highest beta to retail sentiment and liquidity; lags large caps in risk-off.

companies.why: retail broking activity peaks in smallcap booms
demat additions surge in retail booms

NSE:Nifty Midcap 150.means: Nifty Midcap 150: the midcap segment of Indian equities (stocks ranked about 101 to 250 by market cap).
NSE:Nifty Midcap 150.watch: Midcaps outperform in liquidity-driven, domestic-growth phases and underperform when valuations stretch or FPIs sell; their premium to Nifty valuations is the key risk gauge.
NSE:Nifty Midcap 150.links: Moves with retail and SIP flows, India VIX (inverse) and the Nifty / Midcap ratio (inverse).

companies.why: retail trading activity rises with broad rallies

NSE:Nifty Smallcap 250.means: Nifty Smallcap 250: the smallcap segment of Indian equities.
NSE:Nifty Smallcap 250.watch: Smallcaps can fall 30 to 60% in bear phases (2008, 2018 to 2020); froth signs are heavy IPO supply, retail F&O activity and regulatory warnings.
NSE:Nifty Smallcap 250.links: Highest beta to retail sentiment and liquidity; lags large caps in risk-off.

companies.why: retail broking activity peaks in smallcap booms
demat additions surge in retail booms

IND_RES.means: India's total foreign exchange reserves, including gold and SDRs, from the IMF template.
IND_RES.watch: Reserves covering about 10 to 11 months of imports are comfortable; rapid drawdowns signal heavy RBI intervention to defend the rupee.
IND_RES.links: Moves with RBI intervention, FPI and FDI inflows and valuation changes from gold and the dollar.

companies.why: strong reserves reduce currency risk for foreign investors

IN_CPI.means: India consumer price inflation year on year. The RBI targets 4% within a 2% to 6% band.
IN_CPI.watch: Above 6% for three quarters is a formal target miss; persistent readings above 5% rule out rate cuts. High CPI erodes real incomes and FMCG volumes.
IN_CPI.links: Driven by food (about 37% weight in the new base), fuel and core; lags crude oil, the rupee and monsoon outcomes; leads RBI policy and bond yields.

companies.why: keeps policy rates higher, pressuring deposit costs
delays rate cuts that drive housing demand

IN_CPI_FOOD.means: Food and beverages inflation in the CPI, the most volatile and politically sensitive component.
IN_CPI_FOOD.watch: Spikes come from vegetables (tomato, onion), pulses and edible oils after weak monsoons or heat waves; above 8% usually hits rural and lower-income demand.
IN_CPI_FOOD.links: Leads headline CPI; moves with monsoon, food stocks and global edible oil and grain prices.

companies.why: higher food spend crowds out other staples
wheat, sugar and milk costs rise
tea and salt prices rise but margins squeezed
high crop prices lift farm income and tractor demand

IN_IIP.means: Index of Industrial Production growth year on year: output of factories, mines and power plants.
IN_IIP.watch: Growth below 3% signals an industrial slowdown; festival timing and base effects distort single months.
IN_IIP.links: Moves with GDP manufacturing, power demand, core sector output and PMI.

IN_IIP_MFG.means: IIP manufacturing growth, about 78% of the index.
IN_IIP_MFG.watch: Sustained growth above 6% signals a healthy factory cycle.
IN_IIP_MFG.links: Moves with PMI manufacturing, credit to industry and exports.

IN_IIP_CAPITALGOO.means: IIP capital goods growth: output of machinery and equipment, a direct capex indicator.
IN_IIP_CAPITALGOO.watch: Volatile month to month; a 3-month average above 10% indicates strong capex.
IN_IIP_CAPITALGOO.links: Moves with GFCF, credit to large industry and capital goods order inflows.

companies.why: largest beneficiary of the investment cycle

IN_IIP_INFRASTRUC.means: IIP infrastructure and construction goods growth: cement, steel, bricks and related goods.
IN_IIP_INFRASTRUC.watch: Tracks government capex and housing construction; slows during monsoons and elections.
IN_IIP_INFRASTRUC.links: Moves with cement and steel output and government capex.

IN_IIP_CONSUMERDU.means: IIP consumer durables growth: output of appliances, two-wheelers, electronics and similar goods.
IN_IIP_CONSUMERDU.watch: A proxy for urban discretionary demand; strong readings ahead of festivals.
IN_IIP_CONSUMERDU.links: Moves with personal loan and consumer durables credit growth.

IN_IIP_CONSUMERNO.means: IIP consumer non-durables growth: food, toiletries, medicines and other staples.
IN_IIP_CONSUMERNO.watch: Weak readings flag soft mass consumption, especially rural.
IN_IIP_CONSUMERNO.links: Moves with FMCG volume growth and rural wages.

IN_WPI.means: India wholesale price inflation, dominated by fuels, metals and manufactured goods.
IN_WPI.watch: High WPI with lower CPI usually means producer margins are squeezed unless pricing power exists; negative WPI means deflation in goods.
IN_WPI.links: Moves with crude oil, metals and the rupee; leads CPI goods with a lag; drives the GDP deflator.

companies.why: cement prices up, but fuel costs too

IN_GDP_NOM.means: India nominal GDP growth: real growth plus inflation. Corporate revenues and tax receipts grow in nominal terms.
IN_GDP_NOM.watch: Nominal growth below 10% hurts revenue growth, tax collections and the fiscal math; Nifty earnings growth has broadly tracked nominal GDP over long periods.
IN_GDP_NOM.links: Real growth plus the GDP deflator; moves with WPI more than CPI.

companies.why: volume and pricing both follow nominal activity
high nominal growth usually means firm commodity prices

IN_GDP_REAL.means: India real GDP growth year on year, quarterly.
IN_GDP_REAL.watch: Growth below 6% is considered weak for India; above 7.5% strong. Watch the gap to GVA and whether growth comes from consumption, investment or government.
IN_GDP_REAL.links: Leads corporate earnings and credit growth; moves with IIP, GST collections, PMI and bank credit.

companies.why: staples and general merchandise retail tracks household spending
largest beneficiary of the investment cycle

IN_DEFL.means: Nominal minus real GDP growth: an approximate GDP deflator, India's broadest inflation measure.
IN_DEFL.watch: A deflator near zero or negative (low WPI) can make real growth look high while revenues grow slowly; a high deflator flatters nominal growth.
IN_DEFL.links: Tracks WPI more closely than CPI; moves with commodity prices.

IN_GFCF.means: Real growth in gross fixed capital formation: investment in buildings, machinery and infrastructure.
IN_GFCF.watch: Sustained double-digit growth marks an investment upcycle (2004 to 2008); a slowdown signals government capex fatigue or weak private capex.
IN_GFCF.links: Moves with IIP capital goods, cement and steel output and order inflows of capital goods companies.

companies.why: largest beneficiary of the investment cycle

IN_GFCF_SHARE.means: Investment rate: fixed capital formation as a share of GDP.
IN_GFCF_SHARE.watch: India peaked near 35% to 36% in 2007 to 2012; a sustained rise toward that level signals a capex cycle.
IN_GFCF_SHARE.links: Moves with credit to industry, IIP capital goods and corporate capex announcements.

companies.why: largest beneficiary of the investment cycle

IN_PFCE.means: Real growth in private final consumption, about 55% to 60% of GDP.
IN_PFCE.watch: Growth below 5% signals weak household demand; watch rural versus urban divergence and the role of credit.
IN_PFCE.links: Moves with personal loan growth, rural wages, CPI (inverse) and FMCG volumes.

companies.why: staples and general merchandise retail tracks household spending

IN_GFCE.means: Real growth in government final consumption: salaries, purchases and services.
IN_GFCE.watch: Volatile around elections and fiscal consolidation; weak growth means fiscal tightening.
IN_GFCE.links: Moves with fiscal deficit and pay commission cycles.

FPI_EQUITY.means: Net foreign portfolio investment into Indian equities, monthly, in rupees crore.
FPI_EQUITY.watch: Large outflows (more than INR 20,000 cr a month) usually come with a weaker rupee and underperformance of large private banks and IT; domestic SIP flows have offset outflows since 2021.
FPI_EQUITY.links: Moves with DXY and US yields (inverse), India's valuation premium to EM (inverse) and China rallies (inverse).

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly
high foreign holding, sensitive to flow swings

FPI_DEBT.means: Net foreign portfolio investment into Indian bonds, monthly.
FPI_DEBT.watch: Index inclusion (JP Morgan from 2024, Bloomberg) brought steady inflows; outflows widen when the India-US yield gap narrows.
FPI_DEBT.links: Moves with the India minus US 10Y spread and USD/INR expectations.

companies.why: inflows lower bond yields, helping treasury income
lower bond yields reduce funding costs

FPI_TOTAL.means: Total net foreign portfolio investment, equity plus debt plus hybrid.
FPI_TOTAL.watch: Big outflow months coincide with rupee weakness and RBI reserve drawdowns.
FPI_TOTAL.links: Moves with FPI equity and debt; inversely with DXY.

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly

R:NIFTY_GOLD.means: Nifty 50 divided by gold price in rupees per 10 grams: how many 10 g units of gold one Nifty buys.
R:NIFTY_GOLD.watch: A falling ratio means gold is beating equities; long falls (2008 to 2011) came with crises and high inflation. Extreme lows have historically been good times to favour equities over gold.
R:NIFTY_GOLD.links: Moves with real yields and risk appetite; inversely with geopolitical stress.

companies.why: higher gold value lifts loan-to-value headroom and AUM
gold loan AUM and collateral cover rise with gold

R:SENSEX_GOLD.means: Sensex divided by gold in rupees per 10 grams, a longer history of the equity versus gold trade-off.
R:SENSEX_GOLD.watch: Peaks (1992, 2000, 2008) marked equity euphoria; troughs marked gold-led crisis periods.

R:NIFTY_SMALL.means: Nifty 50 divided by Nifty Smallcap 100. A rising ratio means large caps are beating smallcaps.
R:NIFTY_SMALL.watch: A sustained rise signals risk-off and rotation to quality; a long fall signals a broad, retail-led bull market. Turns often coincide with valuation extremes in smallcaps.
R:NIFTY_SMALL.links: Moves with India VIX and FPI flows; inversely with retail and SIP activity.

companies.why: retail broking volumes fade when smallcaps lag
AUM growth slows but large-cap funds hold up

R:NIFTY_MID.means: Nifty 50 divided by Nifty Midcap 100. A rising ratio means large caps are beating midcaps.
R:NIFTY_MID.watch: A sustained rise signals risk-off and rotation to quality; a long fall signals a broad, retail-led bull market. Turns often coincide with valuation extremes in midcaps.
R:NIFTY_MID.links: Moves with India VIX and FPI flows; inversely with retail and SIP activity.

companies.why: retail broking volumes fade when midcaps lag
AUM growth slows but large-cap funds hold up

R:NIFTY_SMALL250.means: Nifty 50 divided by Nifty Smallcap 250. A rising ratio means large caps are beating smallcaps.
R:NIFTY_SMALL250.watch: A sustained rise signals risk-off and rotation to quality; a long fall signals a broad, retail-led bull market. Turns often coincide with valuation extremes in smallcaps.
R:NIFTY_SMALL250.links: Moves with India VIX and FPI flows; inversely with retail and SIP activity.

companies.why: retail broking volumes fade when smallcaps lag
AUM growth slows but large-cap funds hold up

R:NIFTY_MID150.means: Nifty 50 divided by Nifty Midcap 150. A rising ratio means large caps are beating midcaps.
R:NIFTY_MID150.watch: A sustained rise signals risk-off and rotation to quality; a long fall signals a broad, retail-led bull market. Turns often coincide with valuation extremes in midcaps.
R:NIFTY_MID150.links: Moves with India VIX and FPI flows; inversely with retail and SIP activity.

companies.why: retail broking volumes fade when midcaps lag
AUM growth slows but large-cap funds hold up

IN_CREDIT.means: Outstanding bank credit to the private sector, in INR lakh crore.
IN_CREDIT.watch: Level breaks reflect coverage changes; use the growth rate for trends.
IN_CREDIT.links: Grows with nominal GDP plus financial deepening.

IN_CREDIT_YOY.means: Bank credit to the private sector, growth year on year.
IN_CREDIT_YOY.watch: Credit growing well above nominal GDP for long periods (2006 to 2011) built later bad loans; growth below 10% signals weak demand or bank caution.
IN_CREDIT_YOY.links: Moves with nominal GDP, deposit growth and RBI liquidity; leads bank earnings.

companies.why: loan growth drives net interest income

IN_DEPOSITS.means: Outstanding bank deposits, in INR lakh crore.
IN_DEPOSITS.links: Grows with M3 and household savings.

IN_DEPOSITS_YOY.means: Bank deposit growth year on year.
IN_DEPOSITS_YOY.watch: Deposit growth lagging credit for long periods forces banks to raise deposit rates or slow lending, squeezing margins.
IN_DEPOSITS_YOY.links: Moves with M3, RBI liquidity and household savings shifts to markets.

IN_CD_RATIO.means: Private credit to deposits ratio from the monetary survey.
IN_CD_RATIO.watch: High ratios mean banks have little deposit cushion and rely on bonds or certificates of deposit; RBI scrutinises banks with ratios above about 80% on its own definition.
IN_CD_RATIO.links: Rises when credit growth beats deposit growth.

companies.why: high post-merger CD ratio limits loan growth
lower CD ratio gives room to lend

IN_M3_YOY.means: Broad money (M3) growth year on year.
IN_M3_YOY.watch: Growth well above nominal GDP signals ample liquidity, often supportive for asset prices; slowing M3 tightens conditions.
IN_M3_YOY.links: Moves with deposit growth and RBI liquidity operations.

IN_CREDIT_DEP_GAP.means: Credit growth minus deposit growth, in percentage points.
IN_CREDIT_DEP_GAP.watch: A persistent positive gap above 3 pts pressures deposit rates and bank margins; negative gaps mean surplus liquidity and lower lending rates.
IN_CREDIT_DEP_GAP.links: Moves with RBI liquidity and loan demand.

companies.why: strong liability franchise, but margins compress sector-wide

IN_CREDIT_GDP.means: India private credit as a share of GDP (BIS, all lenders).
IN_CREDIT_GDP.watch: India is far below China and the US; this gap is the long-run room for financial deepening.
IN_CREDIT_GDP.links: Rises when credit grows faster than nominal GDP.

US_CREDIT_GDP.means: US private credit as a share of GDP (BIS).
US_CREDIT_GDP.watch: Peaked before 2008; high levels make the economy rate-sensitive.
US_CREDIT_GDP.links: Moves with household and corporate leverage.

CN_CREDIT_GDP.means: China private credit as a share of GDP (BIS).
CN_CREDIT_GDP.watch: Among the highest in the world; stalling credit signals deleveraging and weak commodity demand.
CN_CREDIT_GDP.links: Moves with China property and stimulus.

companies.why: China credit impulse drives steel prices

US_MCAP_GDP.means: US equity market value as a share of GDP, Warren Buffett's favourite gauge.
US_MCAP_GDP.watch: Readings above 200% are historically extreme (2000, 2021, recent); they imply low long-run returns.
US_MCAP_GDP.links: Moves with the S&P 500 and corporate profit share.

IN_MCAP_GDP_WB.means: India stock market capitalisation as a share of GDP, World Bank annual data.
IN_MCAP_GDP_WB.watch: Peaks above 100% (2007) preceded large corrections; readings near 60% to 70% marked cheap markets.
IN_MCAP_GDP_WB.links: Rises with equity prices and IPO supply; falls with nominal GDP growth.

IN_MCAP_GDP.means: Estimate of India market cap to GDP using NSE market cap and the latest GDP.
IN_MCAP_GDP.watch: High readings flag stretched valuations relative to the economy, though rising listings and formalisation lift the structural level.
IN_MCAP_GDP.links: Moves with Nifty and IPO supply; falls when GDP grows faster than markets.

companies.why: rising market cap lifts listing and trading fees

RBI_NONFOOD_YOY.means: Growth in non-food bank credit from RBI's sectoral release, excluding food procurement credit.
RBI_NONFOOD_YOY.watch: Growth above nominal GDP signals rising leverage; a slowdown below 10% hits bank earnings.
RBI_NONFOOD_YOY.links: Moves with personal, services and industry credit; lags RBI policy rate changes by 6 to 12 months.

RBI_PERSONAL_YOY.means: Growth in bank personal loans: housing, vehicles, cards, gold and other retail loans.
RBI_PERSONAL_YOY.watch: Growth above 25% (2023) drew RBI risk-weight increases; a slowdown signals tighter lending standards or weaker demand.
RBI_PERSONAL_YOY.links: Moves with consumption, interest rates and RBI regulation.

RBI_MSE_YOY.means: Growth in bank credit to micro and small enterprises.
RBI_MSE_YOY.watch: Strong growth reflects credit guarantee schemes and formalisation; watch for asset quality stress after fast growth.
RBI_MSE_YOY.links: Moves with GST collections and government guarantee schemes.

RBI_GOLD_YOY.watch: Very fast growth reflects higher gold prices, banks reclassifying agri loans and unsecured borrowers shifting to secured gold loans.
RBI_GOLD_YOY.links: Moves with the gold price and stress in unsecured lending.

companies.why: higher gold value lifts loan-to-value headroom and AUM
gold loan AUM and collateral cover rise with gold
gold loans are its largest book

IN_CORE_CPI.means: Core CPI excluding food, beverages and fuel: the underlying demand-driven inflation.
IN_CORE_CPI.watch: Core below 4% gives the RBI room to cut; rising core signals wage and demand pressure or rupee pass-through.
IN_CORE_CPI.links: Moves with gold prices (personal care has a gold component), the rupee and services inflation.

IN_CPI_INDEX.means: India's CPI index level (2024 = 100), with the older base rescaled.
IN_CPI_INDEX.watch: Comparing the index with its level a year ago shows the base effect: a high base ahead means low reported inflation even if prices keep rising.
IN_CPI_INDEX.links: Year-on-year change of this index is headline CPI.

TRI:NIFTY 50.means: Nifty 50 total return index: price plus reinvested dividends, the correct base for long-run return comparisons.
TRI:NIFTY 50.watch: Dividends add about 1.2 to 1.5 pts a year; rolling 5-year TRI returns below 8% have historically been good long-term entry zones.
TRI:NIFTY 50.links: Tracks Nifty 50 price with a widening gap over time.

TRI:NIFTY 500.means: Nifty 500 total return index, the broad market including dividends.
TRI:NIFTY 500.watch: The standard benchmark for diversified Indian equity funds.

TRI:NIFTY MIDCAP 150.means: Nifty Midcap 150 total return index: the midcap segment of Indian equities (stocks ranked about 101 to 250 by market cap).
TRI:NIFTY MIDCAP 150.watch: Midcaps outperform in liquidity-driven, domestic-growth phases and underperform when valuations stretch or FPIs sell; their premium to Nifty valuations is the key risk gauge.
TRI:NIFTY MIDCAP 150.links: Moves with retail and SIP flows, India VIX (inverse) and the Nifty / Midcap ratio (inverse).

companies.why: retail trading activity rises with broad rallies

TRI:NIFTY SMALLCAP 250.means: Nifty Smallcap 250 total return index: the smallcap segment of Indian equities.
TRI:NIFTY SMALLCAP 250.watch: Smallcaps can fall 30 to 60% in bear phases (2008, 2018 to 2020); froth signs are heavy IPO supply, retail F&O activity and regulatory warnings.
TRI:NIFTY SMALLCAP 250.links: Highest beta to retail sentiment and liquidity; lags large caps in risk-off.

companies.why: retail broking activity peaks in smallcap booms
demat additions surge in retail booms

BOP_CAB.means: India's current account balance per quarter: trade in goods and services plus remittances and income.
BOP_CAB.watch: A deficit above about 2.5% to 3% of GDP has historically been a danger zone for the rupee (2013 taper tantrum).
BOP_CAB.links: Widens with crude and gold imports; narrows with services exports and remittances; drives USD/INR.

companies.why: marketing margins shrink when crude rises faster than retail prices
wide deficits bring rupee and FPI risk

BOP_CAB_XGOLD.means: Current account balance excluding net gold imports.
BOP_CAB_XGOLD.watch: Shows the underlying external position; a surplus here means gold demand alone drives the deficit.
BOP_CAB_XGOLD.links: Moves with oil imports and services exports.

BOP_GOLD.means: India's net gold imports per quarter in US dollars.
BOP_GOLD.watch: Surges in gold imports widen the current account deficit; the government has used import duties to curb them.
BOP_GOLD.links: Moves with gold prices, festival and wedding demand, and duty changes.

companies.why: inventory gains and higher ticket size, but grams sold fall when gold spikes
higher realisation per piece, weaker volumes at very high prices
rural-heavy jeweller, volume sensitive to price spikes
high gold demand and prices support collateral

BOP_CAB_GDP.means: Current account balance as a percentage of GDP, last four quarters.
BOP_CAB_GDP.watch: Deficits above 2.5% of GDP stress the rupee; small deficits under 1.5% are easily financed by capital flows.
BOP_CAB_GDP.links: Moves with crude oil (inverse), gold imports and services exports.

companies.why: rising deficits bring currency risk and FPI caution
rupee weakness from a wide deficit helps exporters
oil is the main driver of the deficit

BOP_GOODS.means: Goods trade balance per quarter: merchandise exports minus imports.
BOP_GOODS.watch: A widening deficit usually reflects oil, gold and electronics imports; it pressures the rupee.
BOP_GOODS.links: Moves with crude oil, gold and domestic demand.

companies.why: marketing margins shrink when crude rises faster than retail prices

BOP_SERVICES.means: Services trade balance: IT, business services, travel and transport.
BOP_SERVICES.watch: The services surplus offsets most of the goods deficit; slowdowns in IT exports weaken the cushion.
BOP_SERVICES.links: Moves with software exports and global capability centre growth.

companies.why: largest US revenue share among Indian IT; client budgets track US activity
about 60% North America revenue; discretionary deals follow US growth

BOP_GS.means: Combined goods and services trade balance.
BOP_GS.watch: A deficit larger than remittances means a current account deficit.
BOP_GS.links: Moves with oil and gold imports and services exports.

BOP_SOFTWARE.means: Exports of telecom, computer and information services per quarter in US dollars.
BOP_SOFTWARE.watch: Includes global capability centres, not only IT firms; slowing growth signals weaker tech spending abroad.
BOP_SOFTWARE.links: Moves with US GDP and tech budgets; supports the services surplus.

companies.why: largest US revenue share among Indian IT; client budgets track US activity
about 60% North America revenue; discretionary deals follow US growth
consulting-led, sensitive to US discretionary spend
mid-tier with high US exposure and digital work

BOP_GOODS_X.watch: Watch petroleum products, electronics, engineering and pharma; falls signal weak global demand.
BOP_GOODS_X.links: Moves with global trade, the rupee and US tariffs.

BOP_GOODS_M.watch: Strong import growth signals strong domestic demand but widens the deficit; watch oil, gold and electronics.
BOP_GOODS_M.links: Moves with crude, gold prices and domestic demand.

BOP_SERVICES_X.means: India's gross services exports per quarter: software, business services, travel and transport.
BOP_SERVICES_X.watch: Services exports have grown faster than goods exports and now cover a large part of the goods deficit; slowdowns weaken the rupee cushion.
BOP_SERVICES_X.links: Moves with global tech spending, global capability centre hiring and US GDP.

companies.why: largest US revenue share among Indian IT; client budgets track US activity
about 60% North America revenue; discretionary deals follow US growth
consulting-led, sensitive to US discretionary spend

BOP_REMIT.means: Net remittances and other transfers, mostly money sent home by Indians abroad.
BOP_REMIT.watch: India is the world's largest remittance recipient; flows fall when Gulf oil incomes drop and rise with a weak rupee.
BOP_REMIT.links: Moves with Gulf economies, oil prices and US labour markets.

BOP_SOFTWARE_YOY.means: Growth of computer services exports year on year.
BOP_SOFTWARE_YOY.watch: Growth below 5% signals a tech services slowdown; double-digit growth supports the rupee.
BOP_SOFTWARE_YOY.links: Leads Indian IT company revenue growth trends.

companies.why: largest US revenue share among Indian IT; client budgets track US activity
about 60% North America revenue; discretionary deals follow US growth
consulting-led, sensitive to US discretionary spend

BOP_FDI.means: Net direct investment flows: FDI into India minus Indian investment abroad and repatriation.
BOP_FDI.watch: Falling net FDI despite strong gross inflows reflects repatriation and IPO exits by private equity.
BOP_FDI.links: Moves with global capex cycles and India's manufacturing incentives.

BOP_FPI.means: Net portfolio investment flows from the balance of payments.
BOP_FPI.watch: Volatile; large outflows coincide with rupee weakness and reserve use.
BOP_FPI.links: Moves with NSDL FPI flows, DXY and US yields.

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly

India nominal vs real GDP growth.means: Nominal and real GDP growth together; the gap between them is the GDP deflator, a broad inflation measure.
India nominal vs real GDP growth.watch: A narrow gap (low deflator) means real growth looks strong while company revenues and tax receipts grow slowly; a wide gap flatters nominal numbers.
India nominal vs real GDP growth.links: Nominal growth tracks Nifty revenue growth; the gap tracks WPI.

companies.why: volumes and prices follow nominal activity

India CPI inflation.means: India consumer price inflation year on year. The RBI targets 4% within a 2% to 6% band.
India CPI inflation.watch: Above 6% for three quarters is a formal target miss; persistent readings above 5% rule out rate cuts. High CPI erodes real incomes and FMCG volumes.
India CPI inflation.links: Driven by food (about 37% weight in the new base), fuel and core; lags crude oil, the rupee and monsoon outcomes; leads RBI policy and bond yields.

companies.why: keeps policy rates higher, pressuring deposit costs
delays rate cuts that drive housing demand

India CPI: food and beverages.means: Food and beverages inflation in the CPI, the most volatile and politically sensitive component.
India CPI: food and beverages.watch: Spikes come from vegetables (tomato, onion), pulses and edible oils after weak monsoons or heat waves; above 8% usually hits rural and lower-income demand.
India CPI: food and beverages.links: Leads headline CPI; moves with monsoon, food stocks and global edible oil and grain prices.

companies.why: higher food spend crowds out other staples
wheat, sugar and milk costs rise
tea and salt prices rise but margins squeezed
high crop prices lift farm income and tractor demand

India WPI inflation.means: India wholesale price inflation, dominated by fuels, metals and manufactured goods.
India WPI inflation.watch: High WPI with lower CPI usually means producer margins are squeezed unless pricing power exists; negative WPI means deflation in goods.
India WPI inflation.links: Moves with crude oil, metals and the rupee; leads CPI goods with a lag; drives the GDP deflator.

companies.why: cement prices up, but fuel costs too

India IIP growth.means: Index of Industrial Production growth year on year: output of factories, mines and power plants.
India IIP growth.watch: Growth below 3% signals an industrial slowdown; festival timing and base effects distort single months.
India IIP growth.links: Moves with GDP manufacturing, power demand, core sector output and PMI.

IIP: capital goods and infra goods.means: Output growth of machinery and equipment (capital goods) and of construction materials (infra goods).
IIP: capital goods and infra goods.watch: Both rising together signals a broad capex cycle; capital goods alone rising points to private and defence capex, infra alone to government construction.
IIP: capital goods and infra goods.links: Leads order inflows and revenue of capital goods and cement companies; moves with GFCF.

companies.why: largest beneficiary of the investment cycle

Private and government consumption, inve.means: Real growth of private consumption, fixed investment and government consumption, the three domestic engines of GDP.
Private and government consumption, inve.watch: Investment growing faster than consumption marks a capex-led phase; consumption lagging GDP for several quarters signals household stress.
Private and government consumption, inve.links: Consumption moves with personal credit and CPI (inverse); investment with IIP capital goods and government capex.

India investment rate (GFCF / GDP).means: Investment rate: fixed capital formation as a share of GDP.
India investment rate (GFCF / GDP).watch: India peaked near 35% to 36% in 2007 to 2012; a sustained rise toward that level signals a capex cycle.
India investment rate (GFCF / GDP).links: Moves with credit to industry, IIP capital goods and corporate capex announcements.

companies.why: largest beneficiary of the investment cycle

India 10Y government bond yield.means: India 10-year government bond yield, monthly average: the benchmark cost of long-term money in India.
India 10Y government bond yield.watch: The spread over the repo rate and over the US 10Y matter. A gap to US 10Y below about 2.5 pts reduces foreign interest in Indian bonds. Falling yields lift bank treasury gains and rate-sensitive sectors.
India 10Y government bond yield.links: Moves with RBI repo rate, CPI, fiscal deficit, crude oil and FPI debt flows; leads corporate bond and home loan rates.

companies.why: falling yields give treasury gains on a large bond book
PSU banks hold large government bond portfolios
falling yields lift bond values but compress new business guarantees
lower bond yields cut NBFC funding costs
bond-funded lender benefits from lower yields

USD/INR, long history.means: Rupees per US dollar from the Fed's H.10 series, used for long history. Rising means a weaker rupee.
USD/INR, long history.watch: Fast depreciation (more than 3 to 4% in a quarter) raises imported inflation, prompts RBI intervention and drains reserves; a weak rupee helps exporters and hurts importers.
USD/INR, long history.links: Moves with crude oil, the dollar index, FPI flows and the current account deficit.

companies.why: dollar revenue, rupee costs: weaker rupee lifts margins
each 1% rupee depreciation adds roughly 20 to 30 bps to margin
large US and export revenue in dollars
US generics revenue converts to more rupees
marketing margins shrink when crude rises faster than retail prices
most marketing-heavy OMC, so most exposed to crude spikes

USD/INR.means: Rupees per US dollar, market rate. Rising means the rupee is weakening.
USD/INR.watch: RBI smooths volatility using reserves; sharp moves come with crude spikes, FPI outflows or a strong dollar. A weaker rupee raises import costs for oil, electronics, gold and coal, lifting CPI with a lag, and raises the rupee cost of dollar debt.
USD/INR.links: Moves with DXY, crude oil, FPI equity and debt flows and the US-India yield gap; inversely with forex reserves.

companies.why: dollar revenue, rupee costs: weaker rupee lifts margins
each 1% rupee depreciation adds roughly 20 to 30 bps to margin
large US and export revenue in dollars
US generics revenue converts to more rupees
crude is bought in dollars; rupee cost rises
aircraft leases and fuel are dollar-linked

INR vs Chinese yuan (CNY/INR).means: Rupees per Chinese yuan. Rising means the rupee is weaker against the yuan.
INR vs Chinese yuan (CNY/INR).watch: A weaker yuan versus the rupee makes Chinese imports cheaper, hurting Indian makers of chemicals, steel, solar modules and electronics that compete with China.
INR vs Chinese yuan (CNY/INR).links: Moves with USD/CNY and USD/INR; yuan devaluations (2015) triggered EM selloffs.

companies.why: a stronger yuan makes Chinese specialty chemicals less competitive

Brent crude in rupees.means: Brent price converted to rupees per barrel: what India actually pays for crude, combining oil price and currency.
Brent crude in rupees.watch: A rising rupee cost hits even when dollar Brent is flat if the rupee weakens; it drives OMC margins, the fuel subsidy and fertiliser costs, freight and CPI fuel.
Brent crude in rupees.links: Product of Brent and USD/INR; leads WPI fuel and the trade deficit.

companies.why: crude realisation rises (capped by windfall tax when high)
marketing margins shrink if pump prices lag crude
crude derivatives are about a third of raw materials
jet fuel is about 40% of costs
synthetic rubber and carbon black are crude-linked

India total reserves.means: India's total foreign exchange reserves, including gold and SDRs, from the IMF template.
India total reserves.watch: Reserves covering about 10 to 11 months of imports are comfortable; rapid drawdowns signal heavy RBI intervention to defend the rupee.
India total reserves.links: Moves with RBI intervention, FPI and FDI inflows and valuation changes from gold and the dollar.

companies.why: strong reserves reduce currency risk for foreign investors

Nifty in US dollars.means: Nifty 50 converted to US dollars: the return a foreign investor earns before hedging.
Nifty in US dollars.watch: Flat dollar returns over long periods while Nifty rises in rupees signals currency drag; FPIs judge India on this line.
Nifty in US dollars.links: Moves with Nifty and inversely with USD/INR; tracks the INDA ETF.

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly
high foreign holding, sensitive to flow swings

Current account balance vs excluding gol.means: Current account balance with and without net gold imports.
Current account balance vs excluding gol.watch: A surplus excluding gold alongside an overall deficit shows gold is the swing factor; policy uses duties to curb gold imports when the gap widens.
Current account balance vs excluding gol.links: Gap equals net gold imports; overall balance moves with oil prices.

Current account balance (% of GDP, last.means: Current account balance as a percentage of GDP, last four quarters.
Current account balance (% of GDP, last.watch: Deficits above 2.5% of GDP stress the rupee; small deficits under 1.5% are easily financed by capital flows.

Goods vs services balance.means: Goods trade deficit against services surplus, per quarter.

Trade deficit (goods and services).watch: A deficit larger than remittances means a current account deficit.
Trade deficit (goods and services).links: Moves with oil and gold imports and services exports.

Goods exports vs imports.means: Merchandise exports and imports per quarter in US dollars.
Goods exports vs imports.watch: Imports rising faster than exports widens the deficit; watch electronics, oil and gold on the import side.
Goods exports vs imports.links: Exports move with global trade and the rupee; imports with crude, gold and domestic demand.

Remittances and other transfers (net).means: Net remittances and other transfers, mostly money sent home by Indians abroad.

India market cap to GDP (World Bank, ann.means: India stock market capitalisation as a share of GDP, World Bank annual data.

India market cap to GDP (World Bank, ann.links: Rises with equity prices and IPO supply; falls with nominal GDP growth.

India market cap to GDP (recent estimate.means: Estimate of India market cap to GDP using NSE market cap and the latest GDP.

US equity market value to GDP.links: Moves with the S&P 500 and corporate profit share.

Nifty 50 / gold.means: Nifty 50 divided by gold price in rupees per 10 grams: how many 10 g units of gold one Nifty buys.
Nifty 50 / gold.watch: A falling ratio means gold is beating equities; long falls (2008 to 2011) came with crises and high inflation. Extreme lows have historically been good times to favour equities over gold.

Sensex / gold (longer history).watch: Peaks (1992, 2000, 2008) marked equity euphoria; troughs marked gold-led crisis periods.
