Gold / silver ratio.means: Ounces of silver one ounce of gold buys.
Gold / silver ratio.watch: Above 80 means silver is cheap relative to gold, usually in risk-off; falls toward 60 or below come with industrial and speculative silver rallies.
Gold / silver ratio.links: Rises with recession fears; falls with strong industrial demand and solar installations.

companies.why: a higher ratio means silver is lagging, hurting its silver revenue

Copper / gold ratio.means: Copper price divided by gold price: growth metal against fear metal.
Copper / gold ratio.watch: A rising ratio signals improving global growth expectations and historically moves with the US 10Y yield; a falling ratio signals defensiveness.
Copper / gold ratio.links: Moves with the 10Y yield, China activity and the ISM manufacturing index.

MSCI ACWI vs S&P 500.means: Global equities relative to the US. A rising line means the rest of the world is beating the US.
MSCI ACWI vs S&P 500.watch: Long cycles of US outperformance (2010 to 2024) reverse slowly; a turn up usually comes with a weaker dollar and helps EM including India.
MSCI ACWI vs S&P 500.links: Moves inversely with DXY and with US tech leadership.

Bank credit vs deposit growth.means: Credit growth minus deposit growth, in percentage points.
Bank credit vs deposit growth.watch: A persistent positive gap above 3 pts pressures deposit rates and bank margins; negative gaps mean surplus liquidity and lower lending rates.
Bank credit vs deposit growth.links: Moves with RBI liquidity and loan demand.

Credit growth minus deposit growth.means: Credit growth minus deposit growth, in percentage points.
Credit growth minus deposit growth.watch: A persistent positive gap above 3 pts pressures deposit rates and bank margins; negative gaps mean surplus liquidity and lower lending rates.
Credit growth minus deposit growth.links: Moves with RBI liquidity and loan demand.

companies.why: strong liability franchise, but margins compress sector-wide

Credit to deposit ratio.means: Private credit to deposits ratio from the monetary survey.
Credit to deposit ratio.watch: High ratios mean banks have little deposit cushion and rely on bonds or certificates of deposit; RBI scrutinises banks with ratios above about 80% on its own definition.
Credit to deposit ratio.links: Rises when credit growth beats deposit growth.

Broad money (M3) growth.means: Broad money (M3) growth year on year.
Broad money (M3) growth.watch: Growth well above nominal GDP signals ample liquidity, often supportive for asset prices; slowing M3 tightens conditions.
Broad money (M3) growth.links: Moves with deposit growth and RBI liquidity operations.

Bank credit to the private sector.means: Outstanding bank credit to the private sector, in INR lakh crore.
Bank credit to the private sector.watch: Level breaks reflect coverage changes; use the growth rate for trends.
Bank credit to the private sector.links: Grows with nominal GDP plus financial deepening.

Bank deposits.means: Outstanding bank deposits, in INR lakh crore.
Bank deposits.links: Grows with M3 and household savings.

India credit to private sector (% of GDP.means: India private credit as a share of GDP (BIS, all lenders).
India credit to private sector (% of GDP.watch: India is far below China and the US; this gap is the long-run room for financial deepening.
India credit to private sector (% of GDP.links: Rises when credit grows faster than nominal GDP.

Credit to GDP: India, China, US.means: Private credit as a share of GDP for India, China and the US, from the BIS.
Credit to GDP: India, China, US.watch: India's low level suggests a long runway for credit deepening; China's very high level constrains further stimulus.
Credit to GDP: India, China, US.links: Levels rise when credit grows faster than nominal GDP.

companies.why: sticky US inflation keeps US yields high and drives FPI selling of Indian financials
higher US prices lift billing rates but squeeze client budgets

US unemployment rate.means: US unemployment rate. Rising unemployment is the clearest sign the US cycle is turning.
US unemployment rate.watch: The Sahm rule: a 0.5 pt rise in the 3-month average above its 12-month low has marked every US recession. Rising unemployment means weaker US consumer and enterprise spending.
US unemployment rate.links: Lags GDP and jobless claims; a rising rate pulls down the 2Y yield and the dollar and tends to slow Indian IT hiring and deal flow.

companies.why: US layoffs and slower spending delay IT deals
collections and BPM work can rise in a downturn, but volumes in mortgages fall

US initial jobless claims.means: Weekly first-time claims for US unemployment benefits, the most timely US labour market indicator.
US initial jobless claims.watch: Sustained readings above about 300,000 have preceded past recessions; a fast rise of 50,000 or more over a few months is the warning sign.
US initial jobless claims.links: Leads the unemployment rate and payrolls by a few months; rising claims usually pull down US yields.

companies.why: rising layoffs signal weaker US enterprise budgets
deal ramp-ups slow when US hiring weakens

US non-farm payrolls, monthly change.means: Monthly change in US non-farm payroll jobs. Positive and steady means the US economy is adding jobs.
US non-farm payrolls, monthly change.watch: Above 150,000 a month is solid growth; below 50,000 or negative for several months signals a slowdown. Strong prints push yields and the dollar up and can hit EM flows.
US non-farm payrolls, monthly change.links: Moves with jobless claims (inverse) and leads consumer spending; big surprises move the 2Y yield and USD/INR on the day.

companies.why: steady US hiring supports IT services demand

US housing starts.means: New US residential construction starts at an annual rate, a leading indicator of US housing and durable goods demand.
US housing starts.watch: Starts fall first when mortgage rates rise; a drop below 1.2 million annualised has marked housing slumps. Housing drives furniture, flooring, home textiles and building products demand.
US housing starts.links: Moves inversely with the 30Y mortgage rate with a lag of 3 to 9 months; leads US furnishing and appliance spending.

companies.why: towels and bed linen sold to US retailers track home sales and moves
mortgage BPM volumes rise with US housing activity

US consumer loan and credit card delinqu.means: Delinquency rates on US consumer loans and credit cards at commercial banks.
US consumer loan and credit card delinqu.watch: Rising card delinquency for several quarters signals a stressed US consumer and usually precedes slower retail spending.

US federal debt to GDP.means: US federal debt as a share of GDP.
US federal debt to GDP.watch: Above 120% the debate on fiscal sustainability, term premium and Treasury supply intensifies; rising debt keeps long-term yields higher than otherwise.
US federal debt to GDP.links: Drives Treasury issuance and term premium (30Y yield); a structural support for gold.

companies.why: fiscal worries support gold, lifting gold-loan collateral
higher gold prices lift value but slow volumes

US federal deficit.means: US federal budget balance as a share of GDP; negative means deficit.
US federal deficit.watch: Deficits above 5% of GDP outside recessions are unusual and add Treasury supply, which pushes up long-term yields.
US federal deficit.links: Inverse of debt-to-GDP changes; wider deficits lift term premium and the 30Y yield.

US manufacturing share of GDP.means: US manufacturing value added as a share of GDP.
US manufacturing share of GDP.watch: A long decline reflects offshoring; a rise would signal reshoring and tariff-led substitution, a headwind for import suppliers and a chance for China plus one suppliers.
US manufacturing share of GDP.links: Moves with US industrial policy and tariffs; relevant for Indian electronics and engineering exporters.

companies.why: China plus one gains vs US reshoring
supplies US industrial and defence supply chains

US net liquidity.means: Fed assets minus the Treasury cash balance minus reverse repo: a rough measure of dollar liquidity reaching markets.
US net liquidity.watch: Rising net liquidity has tended to coincide with rising equities and EM inflows; sharp falls with risk-off periods.
US net liquidity.links: Moves with the S&P 500, Nasdaq and Bitcoin with a short lag; inversely with the dollar.

companies.why: high-beta financial favoured in liquidity upswings

Fed balance sheet.means: Total assets on the Federal Reserve balance sheet. Rising means quantitative easing; falling means quantitative tightening.
Fed balance sheet.watch: QT drains dollar liquidity; markets watch for the point where bank reserves become scarce and repo rates spike, which forces the Fed to stop.
Fed balance sheet.links: Main input to US net liquidity; correlates with the S&P 500, Bitcoin and EM equity flows.

companies.why: global liquidity supports FPI inflows into Indian large caps

US M2 money supply growth.means: US broad money supply growth year on year.
US M2 money supply growth.watch: M2 contracted in 2023 for the first time since the 1930s; renewed growth above 5% tends to support risk assets and emerging market flows.
US M2 money supply growth.links: Leads nominal GDP and asset prices with a lag; moves with Fed balance sheet and bank lending.

US industrial production growth.means: US industrial production growth: factory, mining and utility output year on year.
US industrial production growth.watch: Negative growth for several months signals industrial recession; it hits demand for Indian engineering and chemical exports.
US industrial production growth.links: Moves with the ISM manufacturing index and copper; leads US capex and freight volumes.

companies.why: mining and cement wear parts exports

US high-yield credit spread.means: Extra yield on US high-yield (junk) bonds over Treasuries, a gauge of default risk and risk appetite.
US high-yield credit spread.watch: Below 3.5 pts is complacent; a jump above 5 pts signals stress and above 8 pts recession. Widening spreads usually come with EM equity outflows.
US high-yield credit spread.links: Moves with VIX and inversely with the S&P 500; widening often leads equity drawdowns.

companies.why: global risk-off triggers FPI selling of liquid Indian large caps
wider global spreads raise NBFC funding costs

Corporate spreads, long history: Moody's.means: Baa and Aaa corporate yields over the 10Y Treasury since 1986.
Corporate spreads, long history: Moody's.watch: Baa spreads above 3 pts marked 2001, 2008 and 2020; the Baa minus Aaa gap shows pure default risk.
Corporate spreads, long history: Moody's.links: Moves with HY spreads, VIX and recessions.

US CCC-and-below spread.means: Spread on CCC-rated and lower US bonds, the riskiest credit tier.
US CCC-and-below spread.watch: Moves first and furthest in credit stress; a rise of 3 pts or more in a few months flags rising defaults.
US CCC-and-below spread.links: Leads broader HY spreads; widens with rate hikes and slowing growth.

US investment-grade spread.means: Extra yield on US investment-grade corporate bonds over Treasuries.
US investment-grade spread.watch: Below 1 pt is tight; above 1.5 pts signals tightening credit conditions; above 2 pts stress.
US investment-grade spread.links: Moves with HY spreads but less violently; widens with Treasury volatility (MOVE).

Emerging market corporate spread.means: Option-adjusted spread on emerging market corporate bonds over Treasuries.
Emerging market corporate spread.watch: Widening signals EM risk aversion and makes dollar borrowing costlier for Indian corporates issuing abroad.
Emerging market corporate spread.links: Moves with the dollar, US HY spreads and EM equity flows.

companies.why: regular dollar bond issuer; wider spreads raise refinancing cost

US Treasury yields: 2Y, 10Y, 30Y.means: US 10-year Treasury yield, the global risk-free benchmark for valuing long-duration assets.
US Treasury yields: 2Y, 10Y, 30Y.watch: A move toward 5% has repeatedly triggered equity drawdowns and EM outflows; a narrowing gap to India's 10Y (below 2.5 pts) reduces FPI interest in Indian bonds and pressures the rupee.
US Treasury yields: 2Y, 10Y, 30Y.links: Moves with real yields and breakeven inflation; inversely with growth stocks and gold; leads FPI debt flows into India.

companies.why: rising US yields trigger FPI selling in Indian banks
high-multiple financials de-rate when discount rates rise
neutral on demand, helped if the dollar firms

US yield curve (10Y minus 2Y).means: US 10Y yield minus 2Y yield, the shape of the yield curve.
US yield curve (10Y minus 2Y).watch: Inversion (below zero) has preceded every US recession since the 1970s; recessions usually begin after the curve re-steepens out of inversion.
US yield curve (10Y minus 2Y).links: Steepens when the Fed cuts (2Y falls) or when term premium rises (10Y rises).

companies.why: steeper global curves are read as better for bank margins, but recession signals hurt

US 10Y real yield and breakeven inflatio.means: The 10Y Treasury yield split into real yield (TIPS) and expected inflation (breakeven).
US 10Y real yield and breakeven inflatio.watch: Rising real yields drive tighter conditions and pressure gold and EM; rising breakevens reflect oil and inflation worries.
US 10Y real yield and breakeven inflatio.links: Real yield moves inversely with gold; breakeven with crude.

companies.why: higher real yields usually weigh on gold
higher real yields pull FPI money to the US

Fed funds rate.means: Effective federal funds rate, the overnight rate the Fed sets.
Fed funds rate.watch: The gap between US and Indian policy rates matters for carry trades: a narrower gap makes the rupee more vulnerable and reduces RBI room to cut.
Fed funds rate.links: Leads the 2Y Treasury yield, the dollar and mortgage rates; cuts usually weaken the dollar and help EM flows.

companies.why: higher US rates reduce FPI appetite for Indian financials
higher global rates raise wholesale funding costs
rate hikes slow US spending but strengthen the dollar

France minus Germany 10Y spread.watch: Above 1 pt signals political or fiscal stress in France; spikes can weaken the euro.
France minus Germany 10Y spread.links: Moves with French politics and euro area risk.

10Y yields: Japan, UK, Germany, France.means: Ten-year government bond yields in the four largest non-US developed bond markets.
10Y yields: Japan, UK, Germany, France.watch: Rising yields abroad, especially in Japan, can pull money home from global markets and tighten global liquidity.
10Y yields: Japan, UK, Germany, France.links: Move with US Treasuries plus local fiscal and policy factors.

companies.why: global yield spikes trigger FPI selling

MOVE index (bond volatility).means: Implied volatility of US Treasuries, the bond market's fear gauge.
MOVE index (bond volatility).watch: Above 120 signals rate stress (2022, March 2023 bank crisis); high MOVE tends to tighten financial conditions and widen EM spreads.
MOVE index (bond volatility).links: Often leads the VIX; moves with Fed uncertainty and Treasury liquidity.

VIX (equity volatility).watch: Below 15 is calm; above 25 is stress and above 35 panic. VIX spikes usually bring FPI selling and a jump in India VIX.
VIX (equity volatility).links: Moves inversely with the S&P 500 and with HY spreads.

US 30Y mortgage rate.watch: Above 7% sharply reduces home sales and refinancing; falls below 6% have unlocked housing turnover.
US 30Y mortgage rate.links: Tracks the 10Y yield plus a spread; inversely leads housing starts and home-related spending.

companies.why: high mortgage rates cut US home moves and home-textile demand

US Dollar Index (DXY).means: US Dollar Index (DXY): the dollar against six major currencies, mostly the euro.
US Dollar Index (DXY).watch: DXY above 105 has coincided with EM stress; falls below 100 usually help EM flows and commodities.
US Dollar Index (DXY).links: Inversely tracks EUR/USD and gold; moves with US 2Y yield differentials.

companies.why: dollar strength comes with FPI outflows
metals priced in dollars tend to fall
aluminium prices weaken with a strong dollar

Broad trade-weighted dollar (Fed).means: The Fed's broad trade-weighted dollar index against major trading partners including emerging markets.
Broad trade-weighted dollar (Fed).watch: A rising broad dollar tightens global financial conditions, pressures EM currencies including the rupee and tends to coincide with FPI outflows from India.
Broad trade-weighted dollar (Fed).links: Moves with US real yields and inversely with commodities and EM equities.

companies.why: dollar revenue, rupee costs: weaker rupee lifts margins
each 1% rupee depreciation adds roughly 20 to 30 bps to margin
strong dollar periods bring FPI selling
a strong dollar usually lowers global metal prices

USD/CNY.means: Chinese yuan per US dollar. Rising means a weaker yuan.
USD/CNY.watch: Yuan weakness exports deflation: cheaper Chinese steel, chemicals and electronics flood markets including India.
USD/CNY.links: Moves with China growth, US-China rate gap and trade tensions.

companies.why: cheaper Chinese steel exports pressure Indian prices

USD/JPY.means: Japanese yen per US dollar. Rising means a weaker yen.
USD/JPY.watch: A rapid fall in USD/JPY (yen strength) has triggered global carry unwinds; Japanese intervention is likely near historic weak-yen levels.
USD/JPY.links: Moves with the US-Japan yield gap; inversely with JPY/INR.

EUR/USD.means: US dollars per euro. Rising means a stronger euro and weaker dollar.
EUR/USD.watch: Euro strength usually means a softer dollar, which helps EM flows; it also lifts the rupee value of Europe-earned revenue.
EUR/USD.links: Inverse of DXY; moves with Germany-US yield gap.

companies.why: about 30% of revenue from Europe and UK

USD/KRW.means: Korean won per US dollar, a proxy for Asian tech-export sentiment.
USD/KRW.watch: Won weakness often reflects risk-off in Asian tech and semiconductor cycles.
USD/KRW.links: Moves with KOSPI (inverse), semiconductor prices and the dollar.

JPY/INR.means: Rupees per 100 Japanese yen. Rising means the yen is strengthening against the rupee.
JPY/INR.watch: A sharply stronger yen often signals carry-trade unwinding and global risk-off; it also raises the cost of yen loans and Japanese components.
JPY/INR.links: Moves with USD/JPY (inverse) and Japan yields.

companies.why: royalty to Suzuki and some imported parts are yen-linked

USD/BRL.watch: A carry-trade favourite; sharp real weakness signals EM risk-off.
USD/BRL.links: Moves with commodity prices (inverse) and Brazilian fiscal risk.

companies.why: Brazil is its largest crop protection market; a weaker real lowers rupee revenue

Brent and WTI crude (spot, long history).means: Brent and WTI spot prices since the 1980s. India's crude basket tracks Brent and Dubai.
Brent and WTI crude (spot, long history).watch: Brent above $100 has historically widened India's current account deficit, weakened the rupee and lifted inflation; a WTI discount over $5 reflects US supply gluts.
Brent and WTI crude (spot, long history).links: Moves with global growth, OPEC policy and the dollar (inverse).

companies.why: crude realisation rises (capped by windfall tax when high)
marketing margins shrink if pump prices lag crude
crude derivatives are about a third of raw materials
jet fuel is about 40% of costs
synthetic rubber and carbon black are crude-linked

Brent and WTI futures.means: Brent crude spot price in dollars per barrel. India imports about 85% of its oil, so Brent is the single most important commodity for India.
Brent and WTI futures.watch: Brent above $90 to $100 raises freight and logistics costs, widens India's current account deficit, weakens the rupee and lifts CPI and WPI with a lag; each $10 rise adds roughly 0.4% of GDP to the import bill.
Brent and WTI futures.links: Moves with the dollar (inverse), global growth and OPEC supply; leads India WPI, CPI fuel, USD/INR and the trade deficit.

companies.why: crude realisation rises (capped by windfall tax when high)
marketing margins shrink if pump prices lag crude
crude derivatives are about a third of raw materials
jet fuel is about 40% of costs
synthetic rubber and carbon black are crude-linked

Brent crude vs its history.means: Brent crude spot price in dollars per barrel. India imports about 85% of its oil, so Brent is the single most important commodity for India.
Brent crude vs its history.watch: Brent above $90 to $100 raises freight and logistics costs, widens India's current account deficit, weakens the rupee and lifts CPI and WPI with a lag; each $10 rise adds roughly 0.4% of GDP to the import bill.
Brent crude vs its history.links: Moves with the dollar (inverse), global growth and OPEC supply; leads India WPI, CPI fuel, USD/INR and the trade deficit.

companies.why: crude realisation rises (capped by windfall tax when high)
marketing margins shrink if pump prices lag crude
crude derivatives are about a third of raw materials
jet fuel is about 40% of costs
synthetic rubber and carbon black are crude-linked

WTI crude vs its history.means: WTI crude spot price, the US benchmark.
WTI crude vs its history.watch: WTI usually trades a few dollars below Brent; a wider gap reflects US supply gluts or export constraints.
WTI crude vs its history.links: Moves with Brent, US crude inventories and the SPR; India's import basket is Brent and Dubai-linked, so Brent matters more.

companies.why: crude realisation rises (capped by windfall tax when high)
marketing margins shrink if pump prices lag crude

US commercial crude inventories.means: US commercial crude oil inventories, excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, weekly from EIA.
US commercial crude inventories.watch: Draws larger than seasonal norms signal tight markets and support prices; big builds signal oversupply.
US commercial crude inventories.links: Moves inversely with WTI and Brent prices and with refinery runs.

US Strategic Petroleum Reserve.watch: Large releases (2022) dampen price spikes; refilling adds demand. A low SPR reduces the US buffer against supply shocks.
US Strategic Petroleum Reserve.links: Releases cap crude prices short term; refills support them.

US natural gas.means: US Henry Hub natural gas futures, dollars per million BTU.
US natural gas.watch: Henry Hub sets the cost of US LNG exports; GAIL has Henry Hub-linked LNG contracts, so a low price versus Asian spot is favourable for it.
US natural gas.links: Moves with US weather and LNG export demand; feeds into Asian LNG prices with shipping costs.

companies.why: its US LNG contracts are priced off Henry Hub
regasification volumes rise when LNG is cheap
costlier gas squeezes city gas margins
gas cost is passed through via subsidy

Gold.means: Gold futures price in dollars per ounce. In India, gold is both a savings asset and a large import item.
Gold.watch: Sharp rises raise India's gold import bill and current account deficit; they also boost the collateral value of gold loans and household wealth. Central bank buying has supported prices since 2022.
Gold.links: Moves inversely with US real yields and the dollar, and with geopolitical risk; leads India's gold imports in value terms.

companies.why: higher gold value lifts loan-to-value headroom and AUM
gold loan AUM and collateral cover rise with gold
gold loans are its largest book
inventory gains and higher ticket size, but grams sold fall when gold spikes
higher realisation per piece, weaker volumes at very high prices

Silver.means: Silver futures price in dollars per ounce; half industrial (solar, electronics), half precious metal.
Silver.watch: Silver tends to outperform gold late in risk-on cycles and fall harder in downturns.
Silver.links: Moves with gold and with industrial demand, especially solar panels.

companies.why: India's largest silver producer; silver is a big share of profit
silver paste is a solar cell input

Copper.means: Copper futures price in dollars per pound, a barometer of global industrial demand.
Copper.watch: Rising copper signals stronger global manufacturing and grid investment; it raises input costs for Indian wire, cable and electrical makers.
Copper.links: Moves with China activity, the dollar (inverse) and power grid and data centre spending.

companies.why: copper miner: realisation tracks LME price
copper is the main input; pass-through with a lag
copper used in wires, fans and motors

Uranium miners (URA).means: ETF of uranium miners, a proxy for sentiment on nuclear power.
Uranium miners (URA).watch: Rising prices reflect new reactor plans and supply constraints.
Uranium miners (URA).links: Moves with uranium spot prices and AI-driven power demand narratives.

companies.why: nuclear expansion plans, but fuel cost rises

Wheat.means: Chicago wheat futures, a global grain price benchmark.
Wheat.watch: Spikes (2022) feed food inflation and can prompt export restrictions; India's domestic wheat price is set more by its own procurement and stocks.
Wheat.links: Moves with weather, Black Sea supply and the dollar.

companies.why: wheat flour is a key biscuit input
agri trading gains, but flour costs for foods

Bitcoin.means: Bitcoin price in US dollars, a speculative asset sensitive to global liquidity.
Bitcoin.watch: Big moves tend to track liquidity cycles and risk appetite; crashes often coincide with leveraged retail losses.
Bitcoin.links: Moves with US net liquidity and Nasdaq.

Equal-weight vs cap-weight S&P 500.means: Equal-weight S&P 500 relative to the cap-weighted index.
Equal-weight vs cap-weight S&P 500.watch: A falling line means a handful of mega-caps drive returns; narrow markets are more fragile.
Equal-weight vs cap-weight S&P 500.links: Moves inversely with mega-cap tech leadership.

Emerging markets vs ACWI.means: EM equities relative to global equities.
Emerging markets vs ACWI.watch: EM outperformance usually needs a weaker dollar and strong China; long underperformance followed 2011.

companies.why: EM allocations lift FPI flows into India

India vs emerging markets (USD).means: India ETF relative to the EM ETF, in dollars.
India vs emerging markets (USD).watch: A falling line means FPIs are rotating from India to other EMs, often China, Korea or Taiwan; India's valuation premium to EM drives this.
India vs emerging markets (USD).links: Moves with FPI flows, USD/INR (inverse) and China stimulus (inverse).

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly
high foreign holding, sensitive to flow swings

Apple vs semiconductors.means: Apple relative to the semiconductor ETF: consumer hardware against AI chip demand.
Apple vs semiconductors.watch: A falling line means AI chip spending is outpacing consumer device demand.
Apple vs semiconductors.links: Moves with AI capex (inverse) and smartphone demand.

CoreWeave.means: CoreWeave share price, an AI cloud provider funded with heavy debt.
CoreWeave.watch: Treated as a canary for AI infrastructure financing; sharp falls signal stress in AI capex funding.
CoreWeave.links: Moves with Nvidia, credit spreads and AI sentiment.

Hyperscalers, rebased.means: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta rebased to a common start.
Hyperscalers, rebased.watch: Their combined capex guidance sets the pace for data centres, chips and power equipment worldwide.
Hyperscalers, rebased.links: Moves with AI capex expectations and Nasdaq.

companies.why: largest US revenue share among Indian IT; client budgets track US activity
about 60% North America revenue; discretionary deals follow US growth
Indian data centre demand from hyperscalers

Nvidia and semiconductors, rebased.means: Nvidia, the SMH semiconductor ETF and Oracle rebased.
Nvidia and semiconductors, rebased.watch: Their divergence shows whether AI gains are broadening across chips and cloud or concentrating in one name.
Nvidia and semiconductors, rebased.links: Moves with hyperscaler capex and AI financing conditions.

Major indices, rebased.means: S&P 500, Nifty 50, Nikkei 225 and Hang Seng rebased to a common start, in local currency.
Major indices, rebased.watch: Shows relative performance; India's outperformance over long periods has come with a valuation premium.
Major indices, rebased.links: Global indices move together in risk-off episodes.

Latin America (USD ETFs), rebased.means: Brazil, Chile, Peru and Argentina ETFs in dollars, rebased.
Latin America (USD ETFs), rebased.watch: Commodity-heavy markets; they rise with copper, iron ore and a weak dollar.
Latin America (USD ETFs), rebased.links: Moves with commodities and inversely with DXY.

Small caps vs large caps: Russell 2000 /.means: US small caps relative to large caps.
Small caps vs large caps: Russell 2000 /.watch: Small caps outperform when rate cuts and broad growth are expected; long underperformance reflects high rates.
Small caps vs large caps: Russell 2000 /.links: Moves inversely with the US 2Y yield and credit spreads.

Korea (KOSPI).means: KOSPI, South Korea's benchmark, dominated by memory chip makers.
Korea (KOSPI).watch: A bellwether for global tech and trade cycles; foreigners treat Korea and India as alternative EM allocations.
Korea (KOSPI).links: Moves with semiconductor prices, USD/KRW (inverse) and global trade.

% of stocks above 20-day EMA.means: Share of Nifty 500 stocks trading above their 20-day exponential moving average (short-term trend).
% of stocks above 20-day EMA.watch: Below 20% is oversold and has often marked short-term bottoms; above 80% is overbought. Index highs with falling breadth signal a narrowing rally.
% of stocks above 20-day EMA.links: Leads index turns; moves with India VIX (inverse) and the midcap and smallcap ratios.

% of stocks above 50-day SMA.means: Share of Nifty 500 stocks trading above their 50-day simple moving average (medium-term trend).
% of stocks above 50-day SMA.watch: Below 20% is oversold and has often marked short-term bottoms; above 80% is overbought. Index highs with falling breadth signal a narrowing rally.
% of stocks above 50-day SMA.links: Leads index turns; moves with India VIX (inverse) and the midcap and smallcap ratios.

% of stocks above 200-day SMA.means: Share of Nifty 500 stocks trading above their 200-day simple moving average (long-term trend).
% of stocks above 200-day SMA.watch: Below 20% is oversold and has often marked short-term bottoms; above 80% is overbought. Index highs with falling breadth signal a narrowing rally.
% of stocks above 200-day SMA.links: Leads index turns; moves with India VIX (inverse) and the midcap and smallcap ratios.

% of stocks above 40-week EMA.means: Share of Nifty 500 stocks trading above their 40-week exponential moving average (long-term trend).
% of stocks above 40-week EMA.watch: Below 20% is oversold and has often marked short-term bottoms; above 80% is overbought. Index highs with falling breadth signal a narrowing rally.
% of stocks above 40-week EMA.links: Leads index turns; moves with India VIX (inverse) and the midcap and smallcap ratios.

New 52-week highs vs lows.means: Number of Nifty 500 stocks at new 52-week highs against those at new lows.
New 52-week highs vs lows.watch: Lows exceeding highs while the index holds up signals hidden weakness; a surge in lows marks capitulation.
New 52-week highs vs lows.links: Leads index trend changes; moves with % of stocks above 200-day average.

Advances minus declines.means: Daily advancing minus declining stocks, cumulated.
Advances minus declines.watch: A falling advance-decline line while the index rises is a classic warning sign of narrow leadership.
Advances minus declines.links: Moves with small and midcap performance.

Nifty 500 cash turnover.means: Daily cash market turnover of Nifty 500 stocks in rupees crore.
Nifty 500 cash turnover.watch: Rising turnover in rallies confirms participation; turnover spikes in falls often mark capitulation.
Nifty 500 cash turnover.links: Moves with volatility, retail activity and FPI flows.

FPI net investment in Indian equity, mon.means: Net foreign portfolio investment into Indian equities, monthly, in rupees crore.
FPI net investment in Indian equity, mon.watch: Large outflows (more than INR 20,000 cr a month) usually come with a weaker rupee and underperformance of large private banks and IT; domestic SIP flows have offset outflows since 2021.
FPI net investment in Indian equity, mon.links: Moves with DXY and US yields (inverse), India's valuation premium to EM (inverse) and China rallies (inverse).

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly
high foreign holding, sensitive to flow swings

FPI equity flows, rolling 12-month sum.means: Twelve-month rolling total of FPI net equity investment.
FPI equity flows, rolling 12-month sum.watch: Rolling outflows have marked FPI underweight phases (2008, 2022, 2025); a turn back to inflows has often supported large private banks and the rupee.
FPI equity flows, rolling 12-month sum.links: Moves with DXY (inverse), India's valuation premium (inverse) and global EM allocation.

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly
high foreign holding, sensitive to flow swings

FPI net investment in Indian debt, month.means: Net foreign portfolio investment into Indian bonds, monthly.
FPI net investment in Indian debt, month.watch: Index inclusion (JP Morgan from 2024, Bloomberg) brought steady inflows; outflows widen when the India-US yield gap narrows.
FPI net investment in Indian debt, month.links: Moves with the India minus US 10Y spread and USD/INR expectations.

companies.why: inflows lower bond yields, helping treasury income
lower bond yields reduce funding costs

Foreign vs domestic institutions, monthl.means: Monthly net buying by FPIs and by domestic institutions (mutual funds, insurers, pensions).
Foreign vs domestic institutions, monthl.watch: Domestic institutions have absorbed FPI selling since 2021 thanks to SIP flows; months when both sell are rare and usually deep corrections.
Foreign vs domestic institutions, monthl.links: DII flows move with SIP inflows; FPI flows with global factors.

companies.why: DII buying reflects mutual fund inflows
most affected by FPI flow swings

Mutual funds, insurers and retail, month.means: Monthly net equity buying by mutual funds, insurers and individual investors.
Mutual funds, insurers and retail, month.watch: Mutual fund buying is steady through SIPs; retail direct buying spikes in rallies and can turn to selling at tops.
Mutual funds, insurers and retail, month.links: Moves with SIP flows, market returns and new demat accounts.

Daily: FPI vs domestic institutions, las.means: Monthly net buying by FPIs and by domestic institutions (mutual funds, insurers, pensions).
Daily: FPI vs domestic institutions, las.watch: Domestic institutions have absorbed FPI selling since 2021 thanks to SIP flows; months when both sell are rare and usually deep corrections.
Daily: FPI vs domestic institutions, las.links: DII flows move with SIP inflows; FPI flows with global factors.

companies.why: DII buying reflects mutual fund inflows
most affected by FPI flow swings

Base effect: CPI index vs the same index.means: The CPI index alongside the index from 12 months earlier, shifted forward one year.
Base effect: CPI index vs the same index.watch: The gap between lines is inflation; a rising line ahead means a high base and lower reported inflation for the same monthly price rise.
Base effect: CPI index vs the same index.links: Lets you anticipate headline CPI before the release.

Headline vs core CPI.means: Headline CPI and core CPI (excluding food, beverages and fuel). RBI's target is 4%.
Headline vs core CPI.watch: Headline above core means food or fuel is driving inflation, which RBI tends to look through if temporary; core rising is harder to ignore.
Headline vs core CPI.links: Headline moves with food and crude; core with wages, rupee and gold.

Core CPI (excluding food, beverages and.means: Core CPI excluding food, beverages and fuel: the underlying demand-driven inflation.
Core CPI (excluding food, beverages and.watch: Core below 4% gives the RBI room to cut; rising core signals wage and demand pressure or rupee pass-through.
Core CPI (excluding food, beverages and.links: Moves with gold prices (personal care has a gold component), the rupee and services inflation.

Food and beverages inflation.means: Food and beverages inflation in the CPI, the most volatile and politically sensitive component.
Food and beverages inflation.watch: Spikes come from vegetables (tomato, onion), pulses and edible oils after weak monsoons or heat waves; above 8% usually hits rural and lower-income demand.
Food and beverages inflation.links: Leads headline CPI; moves with monsoon, food stocks and global edible oil and grain prices.

Stocks within 2% of their 52-week high v.means: Number of Nifty 500 stocks at new 52-week highs against those at new lows.
Stocks within 2% of their 52-week high v.watch: Lows exceeding highs while the index holds up signals hidden weakness; a surge in lows marks capitulation.
Stocks within 2% of their 52-week high v.links: Leads index trend changes; moves with % of stocks above 200-day average.

Gold price (USD/oz).means: Gold futures price in dollars per ounce. In India, gold is both a savings asset and a large import item.
Gold price (USD/oz).watch: Sharp rises raise India's gold import bill and current account deficit; they also boost the collateral value of gold loans and household wealth. Central bank buying has supported prices since 2022.
Gold price (USD/oz).links: Moves inversely with US real yields and the dollar, and with geopolitical risk; leads India's gold imports in value terms.

1D return breadth: % of stocks positive.means: Share of Nifty 500 stocks with a positive return over the past 1D.
1D return breadth: % of stocks positive.watch: Below 30% means broad selling; above 70% broad buying. Extremes over 1M and 3M windows often precede reversals.
1D return breadth: % of stocks positive.links: Moves with index returns and India VIX (inverse).

1W return breadth: % of stocks positive.means: Share of Nifty 500 stocks with a positive return over the past 1W.
1W return breadth: % of stocks positive.watch: Below 30% means broad selling; above 70% broad buying. Extremes over 1M and 3M windows often precede reversals.
1W return breadth: % of stocks positive.links: Moves with index returns and India VIX (inverse).

1M return breadth: % of stocks positive.means: Share of Nifty 500 stocks with a positive return over the past 1M.
1M return breadth: % of stocks positive.watch: Below 30% means broad selling; above 70% broad buying. Extremes over 1M and 3M windows often precede reversals.
1M return breadth: % of stocks positive.links: Moves with index returns and India VIX (inverse).

3M return breadth: % of stocks positive.means: Share of Nifty 500 stocks with a positive return over the past 3M.
3M return breadth: % of stocks positive.watch: Below 30% means broad selling; above 70% broad buying. Extremes over 1M and 3M windows often precede reversals.
3M return breadth: % of stocks positive.links: Moves with index returns and India VIX (inverse).

% of stocks positive and median return b.means: Share of Nifty 500 stocks up and the median stock return over several horizons.
% of stocks positive and median return b.watch: A median return well below the index return means large caps are masking weakness in the typical stock.

Distance from 52-week high.means: Number of Nifty 500 stocks by how far they trade below their 52-week high.
Distance from 52-week high.watch: Many stocks more than 20% below highs means a stealth bear market even if the index is near highs.
Distance from 52-week high.links: Moves with breadth and smallcap ratios.

1-month return by size: the smaller, the.means: Mean and median one-month returns by market-cap bucket within the Nifty 500.
1-month return by size: the smaller, the.watch: Small buckets falling more is typical of risk-off; small buckets leading signals risk-on.
1-month return by size: the smaller, the.links: Moves with the Nifty / smallcap ratio.

Market concentration: share of total NSE.means: Share of total NSE market cap held by the top N stocks.
Market concentration: share of total NSE.watch: Rising concentration means a few large stocks drive the market; falling concentration means broad rallies.
Market concentration: share of total NSE.links: Moves inversely with midcap and smallcap outperformance.

Sector risk vs return (3 months).means: Each NSE industry plotted by 3-month return against volatility.
Sector risk vs return (3 months).watch: Sectors with high return and low volatility show orderly leadership; high volatility with negative returns flags stress.
Sector risk vs return (3 months).links: Compare with sector index charts and FPI flows.

Top 10 stocks this month.means: Best one-month performers in the Nifty 500.
Top 10 stocks this month.watch: Leadership clustering in one sector signals a theme.
Top 10 stocks this month.links: Compare with sector risk vs return.

Bottom 10 stocks this month.means: Worst one-month performers in the Nifty 500.
Bottom 10 stocks this month.watch: Clusters in one sector often reflect a regulatory, commodity or earnings shock.
Bottom 10 stocks this month.links: Compare with sector risk vs return.

FPI net investment by calendar year (INR.means: Net FPI investment in Indian equity and debt by calendar year.
FPI net investment by calendar year (INR.watch: Years of heavy equity outflows (2008, 2022, 2025) have coincided with rupee weakness and large-cap underperformance.
FPI net investment by calendar year (INR.links: Moves with global risk cycles and the dollar.

companies.why: largest FPI-owned stock; flows move its price directly

CPI divisions: YoY change at four points.means: Inflation by CPI division at four dates, with each division's basket weight.
CPI divisions: YoY change at four points.watch: Shows whether inflation is broad-based or driven by one division, usually food.
CPI divisions: YoY change at four points.links: Food moves with monsoons; housing and services with wages.

Gold holdings: China, Russia, India.means: Central bank gold holdings in tonnes for China, Russia and India.
Gold holdings: China, Russia, India.watch: Steady official buying since 2022 has supported gold prices even when real yields rose.
Gold holdings: China, Russia, India.links: Moves with reserve diversification away from the dollar and sanctions risk.

Gold holdings: Turkiye, Poland.means: Central bank gold holdings in tonnes for Turkiye and Poland.
Gold holdings: Turkiye, Poland.watch: Large buyers in recent years; sales by Turkiye during currency stress show official holdings can swing.
Gold holdings: Turkiye, Poland.links: Moves with reserve policy and currency pressure.

Largest 12-month changes in gold holding.means: Countries with the biggest net purchases or sales of gold reserves over 12 months.
Largest 12-month changes in gold holding.watch: Broad-based buying signals structural de-dollarisation demand for gold.
Largest 12-month changes in gold holding.links: Moves with geopolitics and sanctions risk.

One sector through time: US share vs Ind.means: A sector's share of US market cap over decades against its share in India today.
One sector through time: US share vs Ind.watch: Shows how sector weights shifted as the US got richer, as an analogy for India.

Real household consumption per head (con.means: Real household consumption per person for India and the US.
Real household consumption per head (con.watch: India today is where the US was many decades ago; the slope shows the pace of catch-up.
Real household consumption per head (con.links: Moves with real PFCE growth and population.

companies.why: staples and general merchandise retail tracks household spending

Where India's sector mix could move: US.means: Sector share differences between the US at India's future consumption level and India today.
Where India's sector mix could move: US.watch: Positive bars suggest sectors that could gain share as India gets richer; a lens, not a forecast.
Where India's sector mix could move: US.links: Structural, depends on the chosen growth path.

Outstanding credit by sector.means: Outstanding bank credit for the selected RBI sector, INR lakh crore.
Outstanding credit by sector.watch: Level breaks reflect changes in bank coverage; use the growth charts for trends.

Non-food credit: credit growth.means: Growth in non-food bank credit from RBI's sectoral release, excluding food procurement credit.
Non-food credit: credit growth.watch: Growth above nominal GDP signals rising leverage; a slowdown below 10% hits bank earnings.
Non-food credit: credit growth.links: Moves with personal, services and industry credit; lags RBI policy rate changes by 6 to 12 months.

Personal loans: credit growth.means: Growth in bank personal loans: housing, vehicles, cards, gold and other retail loans.
Personal loans: credit growth.watch: Growth above 25% (2023) drew RBI risk-weight increases; a slowdown signals tighter lending standards or weaker demand.
Personal loans: credit growth.links: Moves with consumption, interest rates and RBI regulation.

Micro and small: credit growth.means: Growth in bank credit to micro and small enterprises.
Micro and small: credit growth.watch: Strong growth reflects credit guarantee schemes and formalisation; watch for asset quality stress after fast growth.
Micro and small: credit growth.links: Moves with GST collections and government guarantee schemes.

Gold loans: credit growth.watch: Very fast growth reflects higher gold prices, banks reclassifying agri loans and unsecured borrowers shifting to secured gold loans.
Gold loans: credit growth.links: Moves with the gold price and stress in unsecured lending.

Agriculture: credit growth.means: Bank credit growth to agriculture and allied activities.
Agriculture: credit growth.watch: Priority sector targets keep growth steady; spikes before elections or after loan waivers can precede stress.
Agriculture: credit growth.links: Moves with crop prices, monsoon and gold loan reclassification.

Industry: credit growth.means: Bank credit growth to industry: micro, small, medium and large firms.
Industry: credit growth.watch: Large corporate credit was flat for a decade after 2013; a sustained pick-up signals a private capex cycle, though large firms also borrow from bond markets.
Industry: credit growth.links: Moves with IIP capital goods, GFCF and corporate bond yields.

Medium: credit growth.means: Bank credit growth to medium enterprises.
Medium: credit growth.watch: Fast growth after the definition change and guarantee schemes; watch asset quality two years after growth peaks.
Medium: credit growth.links: Moves with MSME formalisation and GST compliance.

Large: credit growth.means: Bank credit growth to large industry.
Large: credit growth.watch: Weak growth can reflect bond market substitution rather than weak capex; strong growth signals private capex funding.
Large: credit growth.links: Moves with corporate bond spreads (inverse when banks are cheaper) and capex.

Services: credit growth.means: Bank credit growth to services: trade, NBFCs, real estate, transport and others.
Services: credit growth.watch: Fast growth has often been driven by bank lending to NBFCs, which RBI has tightened via risk weights.
Services: credit growth.links: Moves with NBFC funding, trade activity and commercial real estate.

NBFCs: credit growth.means: Bank credit growth to non-bank finance companies.
NBFCs: credit growth.watch: Very fast growth increases contagion risk (2018 IL&FS); RBI raised risk weights in 2023, slowing it.
NBFCs: credit growth.links: Moves with NBFC AUM growth and corporate bond spreads.

Credit cards: credit growth.means: Growth in bank credit card outstandings.
Credit cards: credit growth.watch: Growth above 25% has preceded rising delinquencies; RBI tightened unsecured lending risk weights in 2023.
Credit cards: credit growth.links: Moves with discretionary consumption and e-commerce spend.

companies.why: pure-play card issuer: higher spends lift fee and interest income

Housing: credit growth.means: Growth in bank housing loans, the largest retail credit category.
Housing: credit growth.watch: Growth tracks property sales and rates; slowing growth with high rates signals a housing slowdown.
Housing: credit growth.links: Moves inversely with home loan rates and with property registrations.

Vehicle loans: credit growth.watch: Strong growth supports car and two-wheeler sales; slowing growth signals weaker demand or tighter lending.
Vehicle loans: credit growth.links: Moves with auto sales and interest rates (inverse).

Computer software: credit growth.means: Bank credit growth to the computer software sector.
Computer software: credit growth.watch: Small and volatile; IT companies are mostly cash-rich, so growth reflects working capital and smaller firms.

Commercial real estate: credit growth.means: Bank credit growth to commercial real estate developers.
Commercial real estate: credit growth.watch: Fast growth can signal a property upcycle but also rising risk; banks were burnt after 2012.
Commercial real estate: credit growth.links: Moves with office absorption, mall leasing and construction.

Consumer durables: credit growth.means: Growth in bank loans for consumer durables.
Consumer durables: credit growth.watch: Small segment; most durable financing goes through NBFCs, so treat as a signal not a size.
Consumer durables: credit growth.links: Moves with festival demand and NBFC consumer finance.

1-month return distribution.means: Number of Nifty 500 stocks in each 5-point band of one-month return.
1-month return distribution.watch: A distribution skewed to the left with a negative median means broad selling even if the index is flat.
1-month return distribution.links: Moves with return breadth and India VIX (inverse).
